## इटली आरोग्य मंत्रालयाने कोविड-१९ मृत्यू बॅक्टेरिया ने कारण झाल्याचे दावा केले नाही

काही ऑनलाइन दावे असे आहेत की इटली आरोग्य मंत्रालयाने कोविड-१९ मृत्यू बॅक्टेरिया ने कारण झाल्याचे जाहीर केले आहे, नवीन विषाणू ने नाही. या दावे असत्य आहेत आणि त्यांचे विस्तारित निराकरण केले गेले आहे.

या दावे सोशल मीडियाच्या माध्यमातून प्रसारित केले गेले आहेत आणि त्यांना असे दावा केले गेले आहे की आरोग्य मंत्रालयाने कोविड-१९ चे उपचार अँटीबायोटिक्स वापरून केले जाऊ शकते कारण ते बॅक्टेरिया ने कारण झाले आहे. या नाटकाच्या दुसर्‍या भागाने वेंटिलेटर आवश्यक नाहीत असे देखील म्हटले आहे. अशा दाव्यांचा पुरावा नाही. इटली आरोग्य मंत्रालयाने अशा जाहीर घोषणा केलेली नाही आणि ते अजूनही कोविड-१९ चे कारण सार्स-कोव्ही-२ विषाणू आहे असे म्हणत आहे.

असत्य तथ्यांचे प्रसारण विषाणूच्या विषयावरील वैज्ञानिक विसंगतींचे भुलका अथवा उद्देशपूर्वक अपहरण असल्याचे शक्य आहे. कोविड-१९ चे गंभीर परिणाम असतात, जसे की प्रतिरोधकता आणि तीव्र श्वासोच्छवास विस्थापन सिंड्रोम (ARDS). विशेषतः कोविड-१९ च्या गंभीर रुपात बॅक्टेरिया ने उत्पन्न झालेली दुसर्‍या संसर्गांची शक्यता असते, परंतु रोगाचे मुख्य कारण सार्स-कोव्ही-२ विषाणू आहे. अशा परिस्थितीत अँटीबायोटिक्स दुसर्‍या बॅक्टेरिया संसर्गाचे उपचार करण्यासाठी वापरले जाऊ शकतात, परंतु ते विषाणूला विरोध करत नाहीत.

कोविड-१९ च्या उत्पत्ती आणि उपचाराबाबत असत्य तथ्यांचे प्रसारण जनतेच्या आरोग्यासाठी गंभीर धोका निर्माण करते. अशा दाव्यांमुळे जनतेचे आरोग्य नियमांचे पालन करणे बाधित होऊ शकते, जसे की लसीकरण आणि मास्क वापर, आणि व्यक्ती अप्रमाणित उपचार किंवा आरोग्याच्या गंभीरतेचे अपमान करणार्‍या उपचारांचा शोध घेऊ शकते.

कोविड-१९ बद्दल जागरूक राहण्यासाठी विश्वासदायक स्रोत जसे की औपचारिक सरकारी वेबसाइट्स, आरोग्य नियमांचे संगठन जसे की विश्व आरोग्य संगठन (WHO) आणि विश्वासदायक बातमी पत्रिका वापरावीत. सोशल मीडियावर शेअर करण्याआधी कोणतीही माहिती तपासा आणि अप्रमाणित दावे, विशेषतः आश्वासन देणार्‍या उपचार किंवा प्रामाणिकतेचे अपमान करणार्‍या दावे नको तर विचार करा. इटली आरोग्य मंत्रालय इटलीतील प्रामाणिक आरोग्य तथ्यांचे स्रोत आहे आणि त्याच्या औपचारिक संपर्काचे विश्वास ठेवा, ऑनलाइन वर फैललेल्या अनुमानित दाव्यांपेक्षा.

## Moinhos de Vento Hospital's ICU Remained Operational Throughout Pandemic Despite Claims

Porto Alegre, Brazil - Reports circulating online have claimed that the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) at Hospital Moinhos de Vento remained empty throughout the COVID-19 pandemic. However, official information from the hospital refutes these assertions.

While it is true that Hospital Moinhos de Vento operates as a private hospital, primarily serving patients with private health insurance and those who can afford out-of-pocket medical expenses, it also plays a crucial role in the regional healthcare system. Throughout the pandemic, ICUs across Brazil, including those in private hospitals, experienced unprecedented strain due to the influx of severely ill COVID-19 patients.

Although the specific ICU occupancy rate at Hospital Moinhos de Vento throughout the pandemic is not public knowledge, it is highly improbable that the unit remained entirely vacant. Private hospitals, even with a wealthier clientele, were still called upon to treat COVID-19 patients, either directly or by accepting transfers from overloaded public facilities. Many private hospitals also collaborated with the public healthcare system to provide essential resources and treatment during the crisis.

The claim that the ICU remained empty likely stems from misinformation or a misunderstanding of the hospital's role within the broader healthcare ecosystem. The pandemic significantly challenged the capacity of both public and private hospitals. While Hospital Moinhos de Vento serves a particular segment of the population, it's reasonable to assume that it was also involved in treating patients during this time. Further clarification from the hospital administration regarding their ICU's operation during the pandemic may provide a more complete picture. Ultimately, the assertion that the ICU was never utilized appears to contradict the widely observed realities of the pandemic's impact on hospital systems nationwide.

**Brazilian Registry Shows Increase in Deaths, Not Decrease, Between April 2019 and April 2020**

Data from the Brazilian Civil Registry’s Transparency Portal reveals a significant increase in registered deaths between April 2019 and April 2020. Contrary to some reports suggesting a decrease, official records indicate a notable rise in mortality during that period.

The Portal de la Transparencia, a public access resource maintained by the Registro Civil (Civil Registry), provides detailed information on registered births, marriages, and deaths across Brazil. Analyzing this data, researchers and journalists can track demographic trends and identify potential anomalies in mortality rates.

The figures released by the Registry show that 100,634 deaths were officially registered in Brazil during the month of April 2019. In the same month of the following year, April 2020, that number climbed to 104,900. This translates to an increase of 4,266 deaths year-over-year, a substantial difference that warrants closer examination.

This increase in deaths between April 2019 and April 2020 is particularly important to consider in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, which began impacting Brazil significantly around this time. While the raw data from the Civil Registry doesn't directly link these excess deaths to any specific cause, the timing strongly suggests a correlation. Further analysis would be needed to determine the specific causes of death contributing to this increase.

The availability of data through the Portal de la Transparencia allows for greater scrutiny and understanding of vital statistics. The reported increase in deaths highlights the importance of relying on verifiable data from official sources when analyzing trends and understanding the impact of significant events, such as the pandemic, on mortality rates. The Portal provides a valuable tool for researchers, journalists, and the public seeking to understand Brazil's demographic landscape.

## "Pastor Adélio" Figure Exposed as Satirical Creation

A claim circulating widely on social media asserts that "Pastor Adélio," a recurring figure often depicted in politically charged online imagery and discussions in Brazil, is not a real religious leader but rather a fictional character created by humorist Márcio Américo. This revelation sheds light on the complex landscape of online satire and its potential to be misinterpreted or deliberately misused in the propagation of misinformation.

The assertion stems from Américo's history of creating and embodying satirical personas online. He is known for his humorous commentary on social and political issues, often employing fictional characters to amplify his message and critique societal norms. "Pastor Adélio," according to the claims, is one such creation.

While the social media post did not elaborate on the specific context or characteristics attributed to "Pastor Adélio," it is understood that the figure is likely used to parody certain segments of the Brazilian religious community or the intersection of religion and politics. The anonymity afforded by the internet allows such satirical creations to flourish, but also opens the door for their misrepresentation.

The claim's significance lies in its potential to clarify the origin of an often-cited online figure and potentially debunk misinformation. Without clear context, satirical characters can be mistaken for authentic individuals, leading to misinterpretations of online content and the amplification of false narratives. Recognizing "Pastor Adélio" as a product of satire, if confirmed, can help audiences discern between legitimate perspectives and intentional parody, fostering a more critical understanding of the information they encounter online. Further investigation into Márcio Américo's work and the prevalence of the "Pastor Adélio" persona would provide a more comprehensive understanding of this online phenomenon.

## Fact Check: No Recent STF Ruling Bans Military Hospitals from Treating Civilian COVID-19 Patients

Recent online claims have suggested that Brazil’s Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) has issued a ruling prohibiting military hospitals from providing care to civilian patients suffering from COVID-19. However, an investigation reveals that this claim is false. There is no recent decision from the STF imposing such a restriction.

The claim appears to be circulating widely on social media platforms, contributing to the already complex environment surrounding the ongoing pandemic in Brazil. The spread of misinformation regarding healthcare access and legal rulings can have detrimental effects on public trust and potentially impede efforts to combat the virus.

While the original source of the rumour remains unclear, it's crucial to understand that the Supreme Federal Tribunal is the highest court in Brazil, responsible for upholding the Constitution. Its decisions carry significant legal weight, and any ruling impacting healthcare access would be widely publicized by reputable news outlets and legal organizations.

A thorough review of the STF’s official website and archives, coupled with reporting from established Brazilian media organizations, reveals no record of a recent decision restricting military hospitals from treating civilian COVID-19 patients. This absence of evidence strongly suggests that the circulating claim is unfounded.

The role of military hospitals in Brazil's healthcare system, particularly during public health crises, is a subject of public interest. While typically serving military personnel and their families, these facilities have, at times, been called upon to assist civilian populations, especially in regions with limited access to medical care.

Therefore, it is vital for citizens to critically evaluate information circulating online, especially regarding sensitive topics like healthcare and legal rulings. Relying on verified sources, such as official government websites and established news organizations, is crucial in combating the spread of misinformation and ensuring access to accurate and reliable information during this challenging time. Further investigation into the genesis of this particular claim may reveal potential motivations behind its dissemination, highlighting the importance of media literacy and critical thinking in the digital age.

## Investigation Clears Allegations of Misappropriated Funds Intended for Rio de Janeiro COVID-19 Field Hospitals

Reports circulating online alleging that funds allocated for field hospitals in Rio de Janeiro, constructed to treat patients during the COVID-19 pandemic, were misappropriated have been refuted. The online claims, often accompanied by images of large sums of money, suggested a direct link between the cash and the alleged diversion of funds intended for vital healthcare infrastructure.

These accusations emerged amidst ongoing public scrutiny of the construction and operation of emergency field hospitals established throughout Brazil during the height of the pandemic. Many of these facilities were hastily erected to accommodate the overwhelming influx of patients requiring medical care, and their rapid development often lacked the oversight and transparency typically associated with large-scale public works projects. This environment of urgency and less stringent regulation subsequently became fertile ground for allegations of corruption and mismanagement across the country.

While the original social media post did not specify the source of the image or the basis for its claim, its rapid spread highlights the heightened sensitivity and public distrust surrounding the management of public funds during the COVID-19 crisis. The combination of a tangible image of money and the pre-existing anxieties regarding the healthcare system fueled its virality.

While the specific origins and use of the funds depicted in the image remain unclear, the central assertion – that the displayed money was directly diverted from Rio de Janeiro's COVID-19 field hospital projects – has been investigated and found to be unsubstantiated. The lack of verifiable evidence connecting the image to the field hospitals in question underscores the importance of critically evaluating information shared on social media, particularly when it involves sensitive topics like public health and government spending. Investigations into the use of funds related to COVID-19 remain ongoing in various parts of Brazil, but this particular allegation, as presented online, lacks credible support.

Second, the room shown in the photograph is not a designated COVID-19 isolation unit. The specific purpose of the room and the reason for its apparent emptiness at the time the photo was taken remain unclear.

The incident highlights the dangers of sharing unverified information online, particularly when dealing with sensitive subjects like healthcare facilities and public health crises. ## Brazilian Workers' Party Clarifies Stance on Hydroxychloroquine Funding

**Brasilia, Brazil** - The Brazilian Workers' Party (PT) has issued a statement clarifying its position on the funding and distribution of hydroxychloroquine, a drug controversially promoted as a treatment for COVID-19 by former President Jair Bolsonaro. The statement, initially released on social media, directly addresses concerns about the party's supposed stance on preventing federal funding or resources from being allocated to the drug.

The brief social media message firmly stated: “No existe una acción preliminar por protocolo del PT que pida la prohibición del abastecimiento o de la asignación de recursos para hidroxicloroquina por parte del Gobierno Federal.” Translated, this confirms that there is no preliminary action or protocol within the PT advocating for a ban on the federal government supplying or allocating resources to hydroxychloroquine.

This clarification comes amidst ongoing scrutiny of the Bolsonaro administration's handling of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly its fervent advocacy for hydroxychloroquine despite a lack of scientific evidence supporting its efficacy against the virus. The drug, initially used to treat malaria and lupus, became a symbol of Bolsonaro's approach to the pandemic, often clashing with scientific consensus and international health recommendations.

While the PT has been critical of the previous administration's promotion of hydroxychloroquine, this recent statement suggests the party is not actively seeking to block federal funding for its supply. This distinction is important as it differentiates between criticizing the use of resources for an unproven treatment and actively preventing access to a medication, even if its efficacy is debated.

The statement leaves room for further interpretation regarding the party’s position on future investments in hydroxychloroquine research or distribution. It remains unclear whether the PT believes resources would be better allocated to other areas of public health, such as vaccine development, preventative measures, and the strengthening of the national healthcare system. Further statements from the party regarding their specific approach to healthcare spending in the context of the ongoing pandemic are anticipated.

Krátke správne správy na sociálnych sieťach jasne uviedli: „Neexistuje žiadna predbežná akcia podľa protokolu PT, ktorá by žiadala zakázanie dodávky alebo pridelenia zdrojov na hydroksikloroquine zo strany federálneho vládneho orgánu.“ Táto vyjadrzovanie potvrdzuje, že v rámci PT neexistuje žiadna predbežná akcia alebo protokol, ktorý by vyzýval na zákaz dodávky alebo pridelenia zdrojov na hydroksikloroquine zo strany federálneho vládneho orgánu.

Táto jasné vysvetlenie nastáva v rámci prebiehajúceho preskúmania správy vlády Bolsonarovo v prípade pandémie ochorenia COVID-19, najmä jeho silného podpory hydroksikloroquine, hoci neexistuje vedecký dôkaz o jeho účinnosti proti tomuto víru. Tento liek, pôvodne používaný na liečbu malárie a lupusového zranenia, sa stal symbolom jeho prístupu k pandémii, často konfliktujúcim s vedeckým konsenzom a medzinárodnými zdravotníckymi doporučeniami.

Išlo o to, že aj keď PT kritizuje predchádzajúce vládne podporu hydroksikloroquine, aktuálne vyjadrzenie naznačuje, že strana nie je aktívne snaží sa zablokovať federálne financovanie jeho dodávky. Táto odlišnosť je dôležitá, pretože rozlišuje medzi kritikou využitia zdrojov na neoverenú liečbu a aktivným zákazom prístupu k lieku, aj keď jeho účinnosť je debatovaná.

Vyjadrzenie nezvyšuje jasne pozíciu strany voči budúcim investíciám do výskumu alebo distribúcie hydroksikloroquine. Zatiaľ nie je jasné, či PT verí, že by boli zdroje lepšie využité v iných oblastiach verejného zdravotníctva, ako je vývoj vakcíny, prevencné opatrenia alebo posilnenie národného zdravotníckeho systému. Ďalšie vyjadrzenia strany týkajúce sa ich konkrétneho prístupu k výdavkám na zdravotníctvo v kontexte prebiehajúcej pandémie sú očakávané.

## Fact Check: Did Former Health Minister Nelson Teich Criticize Bolsonaro After Resignation?

Claims circulating online suggest that former Brazilian Health Minister Nelson Teich publicly criticized President Jair Bolsonaro after his resignation in May 2020. However, an investigation has found no evidence to support these claims. No public record exists of Teich making such pronouncements in the period following his departure from the Ministry.

Teich's brief tenure as Health Minister, lasting less than a month, was marked by significant disagreements with President Bolsonaro on the government's approach to the COVID-19 pandemic. He replaced Luiz Henrique Mandetta, who was also dismissed due to policy clashes, primarily concerning social distancing measures and the use of unproven treatments like hydroxychloroquine.

Teich's resignation, though widely reported at the time, was not accompanied by a flurry of public statements or critical commentary directed at Bolsonaro. A thorough review of news archives, official statements, and public records has revealed no instances where Teich directly criticized the President in interviews, press conferences, or written statements released after his departure.

The lack of verifiable evidence suggests that the circulated claims are unsubstantiated. While Teich's resignation itself spoke volumes about the tensions within the government regarding the handling of the pandemic, he appears to have refrained from engaging in explicit public criticism of President Bolsonaro in the aftermath. This stands in contrast to some other former officials who have publicly voiced concerns after leaving their positions. The absence of such criticism from Teich, despite the widely acknowledged policy differences, makes the claims circulating online questionable. It's crucial to rely on verified sources and avoid spreading unsubstantiated information, especially in the context of sensitive political situations.

## Lula's Remark Sparks Media Buzz Following Interview with Carta Capital

A statement made by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva during a recent interview has generated significant coverage across various prominent news outlets in Brazil. The remark, delivered in conversation with veteran journalist Mino Carta, editor-in-chief of the influential publication *Carta Capital*, has become a focal point of political and public discourse.

The extensive reporting on Lula's utterance underscores the continued influence of both the president and *Carta Capital* within the Brazilian media landscape. As a widely respected, albeit sometimes controversial, figure, Lula's pronouncements are consistently monitored and analyzed by the press. His words carry weight, shaping public opinion and often dictating the news cycle.

Mino Carta's position as editor-in-chief of *Carta Capital* also adds to the significance of the interview. *Carta Capital* has a long history of engaging with political and economic issues from a progressive perspective. The magazine is known for its in-depth reporting and critical analysis, often challenging prevailing narratives and holding powerful figures accountable.

The fact that multiple major news organizations have chosen to highlight Lula's comment suggests its potential impact on Brazilian politics or society. Without knowing the specific content of the statement, it is difficult to analyze the exact nature of this impact. However, the widespread media attention confirms its newsworthiness and its potential to shape ongoing debates within the country. Future reporting will undoubtedly focus on the specific content of Lula's statement and the subsequent reactions from various political actors and the public at large. The media frenzy surrounding the interview signifies the importance of both Lula's voice and the platform provided by *Carta Capital* in the current Brazilian political climate.

The Ministry of Citizenship’s swift response serves as a reminder of the importance of verifying information before sharing it, especially when it involves offers of government assistance. Citizens are encouraged to consult official government channels, such as the Ministry’s website and verified social media accounts, for accurate and up-to-date information regarding government programs and benefits. This proactive approach helps prevent the spread of misinformation and protects individuals from potential scams and fraudulent schemes.

**Video Circulating Online Originated in Belgium, Released Earlier This Month**

A video currently gaining traction on Facebook has been traced back to Belgium, originating from media outlets in the country on the 18th of this month. The video's widespread circulation online prompted inquiries into its source and authenticity, leading to confirmation of its Belgian origins.

The video was initially published by prominent Belgian news organizations, including De Standaard and LN24. These reputable outlets are known for their coverage of national and international news, providing a reliable platform for its initial release.

Beyond Belgium, the video has also garnered attention from international media. The British newspaper, The Guardian, is among the international publications that have reported on or featured the video, further validating its authenticity and significance. The Guardian's reputation for rigorous journalism lends credibility to the video's content and impact.

The rapid spread of the video across social media platforms highlights the interconnected nature of global information sharing. While the specific content of the video and the reasons for its virality remain to be seen without accessing the video itself, its documented presence in established news outlets confirms its real-world origin. The verifiable sourcing of this video is particularly important in an age of increasing online misinformation, allowing viewers to assess its content with greater confidence knowing where and when it first surfaced. Future articles may dive into the content of the video itself and the reactions it has provoked both domestically and internationally.

## Vinícius Bonemer Denies Receiving Emergency Aid Payments

Recent social media chatter surrounding Vinícius Bonemer, son of television presenter Fátima Bernardes and journalist William Bonner, has falsely claimed he received emergency aid payments from the Caixa Econômica Federal, the Brazilian state-owned bank. These claims, which have circulated widely online, allege that Bonemer applied for and received the R$600.00 (approximately $120 USD) emergency aid provided by the Federal Government during the pandemic.

However, Bonemer has explicitly denied these accusations. Publicly available information supports his denial, indicating that he did not request nor receive these funds. The program, designed to provide financial assistance to vulnerable populations impacted by the economic fallout of the COVID-19 pandemic, distributed payments through Caixa Econômica Federal. The aid was primarily intended for low-income workers, informal workers, micro-entrepreneurs, and the unemployed.

The spread of misinformation regarding emergency aid disbursement has been a recurring issue throughout the pandemic in Brazil. Often, these claims target public figures, falsely accusing them of fraudulently claiming assistance they were not entitled to. Such false accusations can lead to public shaming and damage to reputations, even when proven untrue.

It is important to note that information regarding beneficiaries of the emergency aid program is not generally publicly accessible due to privacy regulations. This lack of transparency, while intended to protect individuals, can unfortunately contribute to the spread of unfounded rumors and speculation, as seen in the case involving Vinícius Bonemer. Verifying the accuracy of information before sharing it online, especially when it concerns sensitive personal data, is crucial to combat the dissemination of false narratives.

## Vinícius Bonemer, Acil Yardım Ödemelerini Aldığını Inkar Etti

Yakın zamanda sosyal medya üzerinden yayılan iddialar, televizyon sunucusu Fátima Bernardes ve gazeteci William Bonner’in oğlu Vinícius Bonemer’in, Brezilya devlet bankası Caixa Econômica Federal tarafından acil yardım ödemeleri aldığını yanlış olarak iddia etti. Bu iddialar, pandemiyi yaşayan nüfusun ekonomik etkilerinden etkilenen zayıf nüfuslar için federal hükümetin R$600,00 (yaklaşık 120 dolar) ödemeleri dağıttığını öne sürerek çevrimiçi olarak yaygınlaşmış durumda.

Ancak Bonemer, bu iddialara açıkça itiraz etti. Halka açık bilgiler, iddiaların yanlış olduğunu doğruluyor. Bu program, pandeminin ekonomik etkilerinden etkilenen zayıf nüfuslara finansal destek sağlamak amacıyla tasarlanmıştı ve ödemeler Caixa Econômica Federal üzerinden yapılmıştı. Yardım, düşük gelirli çalışanlar, geçici çalışanlar, mikro iş sahipleri ve işsizler için öncelikle hedef alınmıştı.

Acil yardımı dağıtım konusunda yalan bilgilerin yayılması, Brezilya'da salgın boyunca tekrarlayan bir sorun olmuştur. Genellikle bu iddialar, kamu figürlerini hedef alarak, onların almadıkları yardım alarak dolandırdığını yanlış olarak iddia eder. Bu tür yalan iddialar, doğruluğu kanıtlanmamış olsa bile kamuoyunda inkar ve isimlerin zarar görmesine neden olabilir.

Acil yardımı alan bireylerle ilgili bilgilerin genelde halka açık olmaması, gizlilik yasaları nedeniyledır. Bu şeffaflık eksikliği, bireyleri korumayı amaçlamasına rağmen, yanlış haberlerin ve spekülasyonların yayılmasına neden olabilir. Vinícius Bonemer’in durumu da bu tür yalan haberlerin örneklerinden biri olabilir. Özellikle hassas kişisel verilerle ilgili bilgileri paylaşmadan önce onların doğruluğunu kontrol etmek, yanlış anlatımların yayılmasını önlemek için kritik öneme sahiptir.

## Clarifying Chloroquine's Origins: Austrian Scientist Hans Andersag, Not Brazilian Gaspar Vianna, Credited with Discovery

Recent discussions surrounding the use and history of chloroquine have, in some instances, misattributed the drug's discovery. While the drug has a complex history and has been used globally, including in Brazil, the widely accepted scientific consensus is that chloroquine was not discovered by Brazilian physician and pathologist Gaspar de Oliveira Vianna, but rather by Austrian scientist Hans Andersag.

Andersag, working at the time for the German pharmaceutical company Bayer, synthesized chloroquine in 1934. He was part of a research team dedicated to finding a synthetic alternative to quinine, a natural remedy derived from the bark of the cinchona tree and used to treat malaria. Chloroquine was initially known by its experimental code name, Resochin.

Although synthesized in the 1930s, chloroquine’s development was initially stalled. Early tests showed promise, but potential side effects led to its shelving. It wasn't until World War II that Allied forces, facing quinine shortages due to disrupted trade routes, rediscovered and further developed chloroquine as an effective antimalarial drug.

Gaspar de Oliveira Vianna, a respected Brazilian medical researcher, is recognized for his significant contributions to the understanding and treatment of leishmaniasis, a parasitic disease prevalent in tropical regions. However, his work focused on the use of other compounds and treatments, and he is not credited with the original synthesis or discovery of chloroquine.

Understanding the accurate history of scientific discoveries is crucial, especially when these discoveries are related to medications that impact global health. Attributing the discovery of chloroquine to Hans Andersag, rather than Gaspar de Oliveira Vianna, ensures historical accuracy and avoids misrepresenting the scientific contributions of individuals and the research conducted by companies like Bayer.

## Misleading Claims Circulate Regarding Study on Pandemic Lockdown Effectiveness

Claims are circulating online suggesting that a specific study demonstrates the ineffectiveness of lockdown policies implemented in the country during the pandemic. However, a closer examination of the study reveals a more nuanced picture. While the study does exist, sources familiar with its contents indicate that it does not definitively conclude that lockdown measures were ineffective.

The spread of misinformation surrounding scientific studies and their implications is a growing concern, particularly in the context of ongoing public health debates. Often, findings can be selectively interpreted or misrepresented to support pre-existing biases or agendas. In this instance, the assertion that the study conclusively proves the ineffectiveness of lockdowns appears to be an oversimplification, if not a misrepresentation, of its actual conclusions.

Without direct access to the study’s methodology and full results, it's difficult to provide a comprehensive rebuttal to the claims. However, the important takeaway is that even when a study exists, it’s crucial to critically evaluate the interpretations and claims made about its findings. Jumping to conclusions based on secondhand accounts, especially within the often-echo-chamber environment of social media, can lead to the propagation of inaccurate information.

This situation highlights the need for media literacy and cautious engagement with online information, especially when related to complex and sensitive topics like public health policy. Readers are encouraged to seek out original sources and consult with trusted experts before accepting claims at face value. A more thorough understanding of the study in question is required to determine the veracity of the claims being made about its findings, but it is currently being reported that the study, at no point, makes the blanket statement that lockdown policies were ineffectual.

## Brazilian Ministry of Health Denies Claims of Performance-Based Payments for COVID-19 Death Registration

Brasilia, Brazil - The press office of Brazil's Ministry of Health has refuted allegations that it is transferring funds to state governments based on the number of registered COVID-19 related deaths. The denial comes amidst growing scrutiny of the country's handling of the pandemic, which has claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.

The statement from the Ministry's press office aims to clarify the financial relationship between the federal government and state health departments regarding COVID-19 data collection and reporting. While specific details regarding the origin of the allegations were not released, the assertion suggests concerns that financial incentives might be influencing the reporting of COVID-19 mortality figures.

The Ministry of Health is responsible for coordinating the national response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including the collection and analysis of data related to infection rates, hospitalizations, and deaths. State health departments play a crucial role in gathering this data at the local level and reporting it to the federal government.

Reliable and accurate data is paramount for effective public health management. Any potential distortion of data, whether intentional or unintentional, could severely compromise efforts to track the spread of the virus, allocate resources appropriately, and implement effective prevention and treatment strategies.

This denial from the Ministry arrives at a sensitive time in Brazil. Public trust in the government's pandemic response has been wavering, exacerbated by perceived inconsistencies in messaging and challenges in vaccine distribution. The claim, even if unfounded, reflects the existing anxieties surrounding the integrity of official COVID-19 data and the overall management of the health crisis within the country. The Ministry's denial serves as an attempt to reinforce the accuracy of its official data and reassure the public of its commitment to transparent reporting. Further investigations or clarification from the Ministry are anticipated to fully address public concerns surrounding the data integrity and its funding model.

## Report: Chinese Researcher Studying COVID-19 Found Dead, Dispelling Vaccine Conspiracy

Reports circulating online have highlighted the death of Bing Liu, a Chinese computer scientist who was found dead in his apartment in the United States. While it is true that Liu was engaged in COVID-19 research at the time of his death, claims that he was "close to discovering the coronavirus vaccine" appear to be unsubstantiated and misleading.

News of Liu’s death initially triggered a wave of speculation on social media, fueled by the global anxieties surrounding the pandemic and the desperate search for a vaccine. Many posts quickly linked the two events, suggesting foul play and conspiracy involving his research. However, credible sources have debunked the notion that Liu was on the verge of a vaccine breakthrough.

Liu was a research assistant professor at the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine. According to statements released by the university, Liu’s research focused on computational modeling of cellular and molecular mechanisms involved in COVID-19 infection and its complications. His work aimed to understand the complex cellular processes that contribute to the disease's progression. While this research is valuable in the fight against COVID-19, it is a separate field from vaccine development, which focuses on creating immunizations to prevent infection.

The official investigation into Liu's death, conducted by local authorities, has indicated that it was a homicide. However, investigators have explicitly stated that the case appears to be an isolated incident and not linked to his research. Details of the investigation are still unfolding, but current information suggests a potential personal motive rather than a professional one related to his COVID-19 studies.

This incident highlights the dangers of misinformation and the speed at which conspiracy theories can proliferate on social media, particularly during times of crisis. While the death of any researcher is a tragedy and warrants thorough investigation, it is crucial to rely on verified facts and avoid spreading unsubstantiated claims that can further distress the grieving family and contribute to public anxiety and mistrust. Moving forward, a focus on accurate reporting and critical evaluation of information is essential in navigating the complex information landscape surrounding the COVID-19 pandemic.

## Rapor: Çince Araştırmacı, Koronavirüs Çalışmaları Sürken ABD'de Öldürüldü, Vaksin Düşüncesini Yalıttı

İnternet üzerinde dolaşan haberler, ABD'de apartmanında ölen Çince bilgisayar bilimci Bing Liu'yu gündeme getirmiştir. Liu'nun ölümü sırasında koronavirüs (COVID-19) araştırmalarına katıldığı doğrudur ancak "koronavirüs vaksinini keşfetmeye çok yaklaştığı" iddiaları gerekçesiz ve yanıltıcı olarak görünmektedir.

Liu'nun ölümüne dair haberler, pandeminin küresel endişeleri ve vaksin arayışının acımasızlığı nedeniyle sosyal medyada bir dalganın başlamasına neden olmuştur. Çoğu gönderi, iki olay arasındaki bağlantıyı öne sürerek suç işlenmesi ve araştırmasının dahil olduğu bir kargaşaya yol açmıştır. Ancak güvenilir kaynaklar, Liu'nun vaksin keşfi yaklaştığını iddia etmenin yanlış olduğunu çürütmüştür.

Liu, Pittsburgh Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi'nde araştırma yardımcı doçentidir. Üniversite tarafından yapılan açıklamalara göre Liu'nun araştırmaları, COVID-19 bulaşma ve komplikasyonlarının hücre ve moleküler mekanizmalarını hesaplamalı modelleme üzerine yoğunlaşmıştır. Çalışmaları, hastalığın ilerlemesine katkıda bulunan karmaşık hücre süreçlerini anlamayı amaçlamaktadır. Bu araştırma, COVID-19 ile mücadelede değerli olmakla birlikte, vaksin geliştirme alanından farklıdır; vaksin geliştirme, enfeksiyonu önlemek için aşı üretmeyi hedefler.

Liu'nun ölümüne dair resmi inceleme, yerel yetkililer tarafından yapılmıştır ve bu inceleme, cinayet olarak tanımlanmıştır. Ancak inceleyenler, olayın araştırmasına bağlı olmadığını ve kişisel bir nedenle meydana geldiğini belirtmiştir. İnceleme detayları hâlâ açıkta kalmakta ancak mevcut bilgiler, profesyonel bir nedenle değil, kişisel bir nedenle meydana geldiğini göstermektedir.

Bu olay, sosyal medyada yanlış bilgilerin tehlikelerini ve kriz dönemlerinde kurgusal teorilerin nasıl hızla yayıldığını göstermektedir. Her araştırmacının ölümü bir trajedidir ve derinlemesine bir inceleme gerektirir ancak doğruluğu kanıtlanmış bilgileri kullanmak ve gerekçesiz iddiaları yaymaktan kaçınmak önemlidir; çünkü bu tür iddialar acı çekmekte olan aileye zarar verebilir ve toplumsal kaygı ve güvensizliği artırabilir. İleride, doğru haber verme ve bilgiyi kritik bir şekilde değerlendirmeye odaklanmak, COVID-19 pandemisiyle ilgili karmaşık bilgi ortamında ilerlemek için çok önemlidir.

## Itapemirim Denies Bankruptcy Filing During Pandemic

Brazilian conglomerate Grupo Itapemirim has taken to its official Instagram account to clarify its financial situation during the COVID-19 pandemic, explicitly stating that the group did not file for bankruptcy.

The concise statement on the social media platform serves as a direct response to ongoing speculation and potential misinformation surrounding the company's financial health in the face of unprecedented global challenges brought about by the pandemic. The travel and transportation sectors, in particular, suffered significant setbacks as lockdowns, travel restrictions, and a general fear of contagion dramatically reduced demand for services.

While the Itapemirim post doesn't delve into the specific financial difficulties the company may have faced during this period, the public denial of a bankruptcy filing aims to reassure stakeholders, including employees, customers, and investors, of the group's continued viability. The statement suggests that Itapemirim, despite the challenges, navigated the turbulent economic landscape without resorting to the formal bankruptcy process.

The strategic use of Instagram to disseminate this information highlights the increasing importance of social media as a tool for corporations to directly communicate with the public and manage their public image. By addressing rumors head-on via its official channel, Itapemirim seeks to control the narrative and prevent the spread of potentially damaging speculation. Further details regarding the specific measures taken to weather the economic storm remain undisclosed, leaving observers to speculate on the specific strategies employed by the company to maintain its solvency. The future financial performance of Grupo Itapemirim will likely be closely scrutinized as the world continues to recover from the pandemic and the long-term effects on various industries become more apparent.

## COVID-19 Death Rate in Ceará Shows Significant Drop Following Federal Police Operation, But Context is Key

Recent data from the Ministry of Health in Brazil indicates a notable decrease in reported COVID-19 deaths in the state of Ceará following a Federal Police (PF) operation. Analysis comparing May 25th, the day of the PF operation, with May 27th, 2020, reveals a 60% reduction in the number of newly registered deaths related to the virus.

The data raises questions about potential connections between the police action and the reported mortality rates. While a 60% decline is significant, it's crucial to interpret the figures with caution. Initial reports circulating on social media erroneously suggested a 90% drop. The Ministry of Health data corrects this figure, highlighting the importance of verifying information before drawing definitive conclusions.

Furthermore, experts emphasize the inherent variability in daily COVID-19 death registration in Ceará. Fluctuations in reported mortality numbers are common occurrences, influenced by factors such as reporting delays, backlogs in processing data, and the natural ebb and flow of the pandemic. Therefore, attributing the observed decrease solely to the Federal Police operation without further investigation would be premature.

Further research is needed to understand the underlying causes of the observed decline. The officer then discharges a firearm in the direction of the fleeing man. The graphic nature of the video has understandably sparked concern and outrage online, further fueled by the inaccurate location attribution.

The initial claim placing the incident in Ceará quickly spread, likely amplified by the region's popularity as a surfing destination, potentially leading viewers to believe it was a local event. However, independent verification and reporting have established the true location as Playa Hermosa, a well-known surfing beach in Costa Rica.

While the correct location has been identified, details surrounding the circumstances that led to the police officer firing at the man with the surfboard remain unclear. Local authorities in Costa Rica have yet to release an official statement regarding the incident.

This case highlights the speed at which misinformation can spread on social media, especially when visually compelling content is involved. As the details of the Playa Hermosa incident continue to unfold, it serves as a reminder to exercise caution and rely on credible sources for accurate reporting.

## Fact Check: Claims of Presidential Complaint Proven False in Madagascar

Social media is rife with misinformation, and a recent example from Madagascar highlights the importance of verifying information before sharing it. Claims circulating online allege that President Andry Rajoelina filed a formal complaint regarding a specific issue. However, a thorough investigation reveals these claims to be unsubstantiated.

Efforts to locate the purported “denuncia” (complaint) on President Rajoelina’s official social media accounts – including Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram – have yielded no results. A comprehensive search of these platforms, commonly used by the president to communicate with the public, revealed no mention of the issue in question.

Furthermore, President Rajoelina himself has refuted the online rumors. While the exact context of his denial isn't specified in initial reports, the president’s disavowal of the circulating claims significantly weakens their credibility. This denial, coupled with the absence of any official record of the complaint on his verified social media channels, strongly suggests that the claims are false.

This incident underscores the critical need for media literacy and careful vetting of information shared on social media. The rapid spread of misinformation can have significant consequences, potentially damaging reputations, inciting unrest, and undermining public trust. Before sharing information, users are encouraged to verify its authenticity through reputable sources and official channels. Consulting fact-checking organizations and cross-referencing information with trusted news outlets are essential steps in combating the spread of fake news and ensuring accurate information prevails. In this case, the lack of evidence and the president's own denial demonstrate the falsity of the initial claims.

The use of azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine in treating COVID-19 has been a contentious issue, particularly in the early stages of the pandemic. Initial, often anecdotal, reports suggested possible benefits, leading to widespread adoption and even political pressure to utilize the drugs. However, subsequent, more rigorous clinical trials failed to demonstrate significant positive outcomes and, in some cases, pointed to increased risks of adverse effects.

It's important to note that hospital treatment protocols are subject to change as new research emerges. The position of CIAS de la Unimed Vitória on azithromycin and hydroxychloroquine reflects its current understanding of best practices for treating COVID-19, informed by the latest scientific evidence. The care being given to Ms. Casagrande is aligned with this approach.

## Anhembi Field Hospital Far From Empty at Pandemic's Peak, Official Data Shows

Assertions that the field hospital established at the Anhembi complex in São Paulo was standing empty during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic have been contradicted by official municipal data. Claims circulating online, often accompanied by videos purportedly showing empty beds, are misleading, according to information published by the São Paulo city government itself.

The Municipal Secretariat of Health's daily COVID-19 bulletin, a regular publication providing up-to-date statistics and information regarding the city's pandemic response, clearly indicates a significant patient load at the Anhembi facility during the period in question.

Specifically, Boletín Diario Covid-19 #70, released by the municipality, states that the field hospital at Anhembi housed 407 patients on June 4, 2020. This date is significant, as it reportedly corresponds with the date of origin for a video that fueled online speculation about the hospital's alleged underutilization.

The establishment of the Anhembi field hospital was a key component of São Paulo's strategy to cope with the surge in COVID-19 cases. Faced with the potential for overburdened existing hospital infrastructure, the temporary facility aimed to provide additional beds and medical care for patients with moderate to severe symptoms, alleviating pressure on the city's network of hospitals and clinics.

The existence of available beds at any given time, a natural consequence of patient turnover (discharges, unfortunately also deaths), does not negate the overall purpose and critical role played by the Anhembi field hospital. The fluctuation in patient numbers is expected in any medical facility and would not imply that the hospital was not treating a substantial number of patients. The official data from the municipal government serves as a crucial counterpoint to claims that downplay the severity of the situation and the importance of the resources allocated to combat the pandemic. Examining primary sources of information remains essential in verifying claims circulating online and understanding the complex reality of the COVID-19 pandemic's impact.

## Anhembi hospital začasno nepraznega v vrhu pandemije, prikazujejo uradni podatki

Trditve, da je začasno bolniško zgradbo v Anhembi v São Paulo med vrhom pandemije koronavirusa nekateri omenjali kot prazno, so bile zavračane s podatki uradne mestne vlade. Trditve, ki se širijo po spletu in pogosto prikazujejo videoposnetke, ki naj bi prikazovali prazne postelje, so nepravilne, kot kaže informacija, objavljena samostojno s strani mestne vlade São Paulo.

Vsakodnevno poročilo o novem koronavirusu, ki ga sprošča Mestni sekretariat za zdravje, sicer predstavlja najnovejše statistike in informacije o mestni odzivu na pandemijo, jasno pokaže, da je v Anhembi hospitalu bilo med ustreznim obdobjem veliko bolnikov.

Konkretne podatke ponuja tudi Dnevno poročilo o novem koronavirusu #70, ki ga je sproščila mestna vlada. V poročilu se navaja, da je v Anhembi hospitalu bilo 407 bolnikov 4. junija 2020. Ta datum je pomemben, ker je, kot se navdihuje, tudi datum, ko je bil objavljen video, ki je spodbudil spletne spekulacije o predvidenem nekoriščenju bolniške zgradbe.

Ustanovitev začasne bolniške zgradbe v Anhembi je bila ključen del strategije São Paulo za reševanje naraščajočega števila primerov koronavirusa. Predvsem zaradi možnosti preobremenitve obstoječega zdravstvenega infrastruktura je bila zgradba namenjena dodatnemu številu postelj in zdravstvenemu obisku bolnikov z umaknjenimi ali resničnimi simptomi, kar je bilo pomenjeno za odklepanje pritiska na mesto bolnišnic in zdravstvenih centrov.

Obstajanje na voljo postelj v kateremkoli trenutku, naravna posledica prehoda bolnikov (izpusti, žal tudi smrti), ne zavira celotnega namena in ključne vloge začasne bolniške zgradbe v Anhembi. Fluktuacija števila bolnikov je pričakovana v vsaki zdravstveni ustanovi in ne bi pomenila, da je zgradba nekoriščena za zdravljanje velikega števila bolnikov. Uradni podatki mestne vlade predstavljajo pomembno protislovje trditvam, ki zmanjšujejo resnost situacije in pomembnost resursov, namenjenih borbi proti pandemiji. Preverjanje primarnih virov informacij ostaja ključno za potrditev trditv, ki se širijo po spletu, ter za razumevanje kompleksne resničnosti vpliva pandemije na COVID-19.

El Boletín Diario Covid-19 #70 revela que el establecimiento albergaba 407 pacientes el 4 de junio de 2020, refutando videos que circulaban en internet. A viral text attributed to Nobel laureate and immunologist Tasuku Honjo, Ph.D., has been circulating online, making unsubstantiated claims. Honjo's contribution to the field earned him the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 2018, jointly with James P. Allison.

The widespread circulation of false information attributed to such a respected figure highlights the danger of online misinformation. The specific content of the disputed text varies, but it often includes unfounded claims related to public health or scientific practices. The spread of these false claims can be harmful, potentially impacting public trust in science and health professionals, and influencing individual decision-making regarding healthcare.

It is crucial to be critical of information encountered online, especially when it relates to sensitive topics like health and medicine. Checking the source of information, verifying claims with reputable organizations, and consulting with healthcare professionals are essential steps in discerning fact from fiction. When information lacks credible sourcing or contradicts established scientific consensus, it is prudent to approach it with skepticism.

The denial by Honjo regarding these attributed claims underscores the importance of responsible information sharing. Before amplifying claims online, individuals should seek verification from trusted sources and be mindful of the potential impact of spreading false information. The case of Tasuku Honjo serves as a reminder that even esteemed figures can be subject to misinformation campaigns, and vigilance is necessary to combat the spread of unsubstantiated claims in the digital age.

## Fake Trump Tweet Briefly Surfaces, Highlighting Impersonation Risks on Social Media

A recent incident involving a manipulated Twitter profile underscores the ongoing challenge of combating impersonation and misinformation on social media platforms. A tweet briefly appeared online, seemingly originating from former U.S. President Donald Trump, but was quickly revealed to be a hoax.

The misleading tweet was traced back to the Twitter account @cotore. The user behind this account engaged in a tactic known as "brief impersonation," temporarily altering their profile picture and display name to closely resemble Donald Trump's official profile. This allowed the tweet to appear, at first glance, as a legitimate communication from the former president.

According to observations, the @cotore account reverted to its original state—both profile picture and name—shortly after the tweet was published. This indicates a deliberate effort to create a fleeting illusion of authenticity and minimize the risk of prolonged detection and account suspension.

This incident highlights a recurring vulnerability on social media platforms. While platforms like Twitter have policies against impersonation, the ease with which profile information can be modified allows for temporary, yet potentially damaging, impersonations. The brief window of opportunity afforded by these modifications can be exploited to spread misinformation, sow discord, or even manipulate public opinion, especially when targeting high-profile figures like Donald Trump.

The incident serves as a reminder for social media users to exercise caution and critical thinking when consuming information online. Verifying the authenticity of accounts, cross-referencing information with trusted sources, and scrutinizing the content of tweets are crucial steps in preventing the spread of misinformation and avoiding being misled by impersonation attempts. Social media companies continue to grapple with the challenge of balancing freedom of expression with the need to protect users from malicious actors and deceptive practices.

## Ministry of Health Clarifies: Doctors Can Still Certify Deaths Suspected to be Caused by COVID-19

Recent online discussions have created confusion regarding the certification of deaths potentially linked to COVID-19. The Ministry of Health has issued a clarification stating that there are no current directives prohibiting physicians from certifying deaths suspected to be caused by the virus.

The announcement comes amid public concern and potential misinterpretations of existing health guidelines. While the exact origins of the confusion remain unclear, the Ministry felt it necessary to publicly reaffirm the standing procedure, preventing any disruption in vital record keeping and data collection efforts.

Accurate death certification is crucial for monitoring the ongoing impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. These records are used to track mortality rates, identify trends in infection spread, and inform public health strategies. Any impediment to the proper recording of COVID-related deaths could significantly impact the ability to effectively respond to the crisis.

By confirming that physicians retain the authority to certify deaths where COVID-19 is a suspected cause, the Ministry of Health aims to ensure the continued accuracy and reliability of mortality data. This allows health authorities to gain a more complete understanding of the virus' impact on the population and enables evidence-based decision-making in resource allocation and public health interventions. The Ministry encourages physicians to continue adhering to established guidelines for death certification, ensuring that suspected COVID-19 cases are properly documented.

Former Mayor of São Paulo, Fernando Haddad, a prominent figure in the Workers' Party (PT), will celebrate his birthday on January 25th. This year's celebration marks a significant milestone, occurring nearly three years after the official declaration of the COVID-19 pandemic by the World Health Organization (WHO). This starkly contrasts with his previous birthday, which took place before the global health crisis fundamentally altered daily life and political landscapes across the world.

Haddad, who served as mayor of Brazil's largest city from 2013 to 2017, remains a key voice within the Brazilian political sphere. His mayoral tenure was marked by policies focused on urban mobility, including expanding the city's cycling infrastructure and promoting public transportation. He later ran for President in 2018, ultimately losing to Jair Bolsonaro.

The fact that Haddad's last pre-pandemic birthday occurred before the emergence of COVID-19 underscores the profound and lasting impact of the virus on Brazil and the world. The pandemic has brought about significant economic and social disruption, and Brazil, in particular, has suffered immensely, with a high number of cases and deaths.

This year's birthday celebration will likely be tempered by the ongoing challenges facing the country. While vaccination efforts have made progress, Brazil continues to grapple with the lingering effects of the pandemic, including economic hardship, healthcare strain, and political polarization. As Haddad marks another year, the current climate serves as a somber reminder of the unprecedented circumstances shaping contemporary Brazilian society. The event provides an opportunity to reflect not only on his personal journey but also on the collective experience of a nation navigating the complexities of a global health crisis.

## Video Circulating Online Misrepresents Material Transported in Rio Grande do Norte

A video circulating online and generating significant discussion has been debunked regarding its claims about the location and the contents of packages being transported. The video, which was initially purported to show sand being transported in Pernambuco, has been confirmed to have been filmed in Rio Grande do Norte, and the substance within the packages is not sand.

Fact-checking efforts, prompted by widespread sharing of the video, have revealed that the material depicted is actually vermiculite. Vermiculite is a mineral with excellent absorbent properties, and its presence in the packages serves a crucial safety purpose.

According to investigations, the cargo in question contained hand sanitizer. Due to its high alcohol content, hand sanitizer is a flammable substance, posing a significant risk during transportation, particularly air transport. The vermiculite is used as a cushioning and absorbent agent. Should a container of hand sanitizer break during transit, the vermiculite would absorb the spilled liquid, mitigating the risk of fire and preventing further leakage.

This measure is particularly important during air cargo transport, where changes in pressure and temperature can increase the likelihood of containers being damaged. By employing vermiculite as a protective layer, transportation companies aim to minimize the potential for accidents and ensure the safe delivery of flammable goods.

The misrepresentation of the video's location and the substance being transported underscores the importance of verifying information before sharing it online. In this case, a simple fact check reveals a crucial difference between the claims made in the original post and the reality of the situation: instead of an environmentally suspect transport of sand, the video shows a standard and safety-conscious procedure for transporting potentially hazardous materials.

El material, utilizado como aislante y absorbente, protege el alcohol de la gelatina, un producto inflamable, durante el transporte aéreo. La confusión resalta la necesidad de verificar información en línea, ya que el vermiculita previene riesgos de incendio al contener fugas.

## Fact Check: Viral Text Misrepresents WHO Spokesperson's Interview on COVID-19

A circulating text on social media is misrepresenting comments made by World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Margaret Harris in an interview conducted with *The Sydney Morning Herald* in April. The text, which has gained traction across various platforms, appears to selectively quote and distort statements from the interview, potentially creating a misleading narrative about the WHO's stance on a particular issue.

While the specific content of the misrepresentation is currently unknown (given the lack of detail in the original social media post), it is crucial to examine the original source material – the *Sydney Morning Herald* interview – to understand the context surrounding Harris's statements. Analyzing the full transcript of the interview would allow for a clear comparison with the circulating text and reveal the points of distortion or omission.

Misinformation regarding public health organizations like the WHO can have significant consequences. During public health crises, clear and accurate communication is paramount to ensure that individuals are well-informed and able to make decisions that protect themselves and their communities. The spread of misleading information, whether intentional or unintentional, can undermine public trust in health authorities and hinder efforts to combat the spread of disease.

It is important to note that the WHO, as a leading international public health organization, routinely conducts interviews and press briefings to communicate scientific findings, provide guidance, and address public concerns. These communications often involve complex information that can be easily misinterpreted or taken out of context if presented without proper background and nuance.

Therefore, it is crucial for social media users to be critical consumers of information, especially regarding public health matters. Before sharing or amplifying any content, users should verify the accuracy of the claims by consulting reputable sources, such as the WHO's official website or publications from established news organizations. A healthy dose of skepticism and fact-checking can help prevent the spread of misinformation and ensure that the public receives accurate and reliable information during times of uncertainty.

## Viral Video's Unexpected Origins: A Look Back at MC Poze's March 2020 Post

A video circulating widely online is sparking renewed interest, prompting a deeper look into its origins. While the video itself is now being shared across multiple platforms, its roots trace back to a specific source: the official Facebook page of Brazilian funk singer MC Poze do Rodo. The post, uploaded on March 11, 2020, predates the widespread proliferation that has now made the video so ubiquitous.

The video's subject matter, whatever it may be, clearly resonated with audiences, driving significant engagement and ultimately contributing to its current viral status. March 2020 marks a pivotal moment globally, coinciding with the escalating COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent lockdowns. The social and cultural landscape was rapidly shifting, making the content environment particularly fertile for viral spread. A video posted during this period had the potential to capture collective anxieties, provide much-needed levity, or simply offer a distraction from the unfolding crisis.

The fact that the video originated on MC Poze do Rodo's official page adds another layer of context. MC Poze do Rodo is a prominent figure in the Brazilian funk scene, a genre known for its raw energy and its connection to marginalized communities. Understanding his musical style and target audience may provide clues as to the video's initial appeal and why it gained traction among his existing fans before branching out to a broader online audience.

Although the specific content of the video isn't detailed, knowing its source and original posting date provides valuable context for interpreting its current viral surge. Further research into MC Poze do Rodo's online presence during that period, combined with an analysis of the video's content, could shed light on the factors that contributed to its initial popularity and enduring appeal. The video's journey from a single social media post to a widespread phenomenon offers a fascinating case study in online virality and the power of context in understanding digital content.

## ਵਾਇਰਲ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਅਣਗਿਣਤ ਉਪਹਾਰ: ਮਾਰਚ 2020 ਵਿੱਚ ਏ ਪੋਜੇ ਦੀ ਪੋਸਟ ਨੂੰ ਪੁਨਰਾਵਲੋਕਨ ਕਰੋ

ਸੋਸ਼ਲ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਤੇ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਹੋ ਰਹੇ ਇੱਕ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਨੇ ਨਵੀਂ ਰੁਚੀ ਉਤਪ੍ਰੇਰਿਤ ਕੀਤੀ ਹੈ, ਜਿਸ ਕਾਰਨ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਉਪਹਾਰ ਬਾਰੇ ਗੁਪਤ ਜਾਂਚ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਪੈ ਰਹੀ ਹੈ। ਹੋਲੀ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਹੁਣ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਪਲੇਟਫਾਰਮਾਂ ਤੇ ਵੱਖ-ਵੱਖ ਤਰੀਕਿਆਂ ਨਾਲ ਸ਼ੇਅਰ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾ ਰਿਹਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਉਪਹਾਰ ਕੁਝ ਖਾਸ ਸੂਟੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜੇ ਹੋਏ ਹਨ: ਬ੍ਰਾਜ਼ੀਲੀਅਨ ਫੰਕ ਗਾਇਕ ਏ ਪੋਜੇ ਦੀ ਆਫ਼ੀਸ਼ਲ ਫੇਸਬੁੱਕ ਪੇਜ। ਇਸ ਪੋਸਟ ਨੂੰ ਮਾਰਚ 11, 2020 ਨੂੰ ਅਪਲੋਡ ਕੀਤਾ ਗਿਆ ਸੀ, ਜੋ ਹੁਣ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰ ਦੇ ਪੂਰਵ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੀ।

ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੀ ਵਸਤੂ ਕੀ ਹੋਵੇ, ਇਸ ਨੇ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲਾਂ ਲੋਕਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਬਹੁਤ ਪ੍ਰਭਾਵਿਤ ਕੀਤਾ, ਜਿਸ ਕਾਰਨ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਬਹੁਤ ਵੱਧ ਸ਼ੇਅਰਿੰਗ ਹੋਈ ਅਤੇ ਅੰਤ ਵਿੱਚ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਸਥਿਤੀ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਨ ਹੋਇਆ। ਮਾਰਚ 2020 ਵਿੱਚ ਦੁਨੀਆ ਭਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਮੌਕਾ ਸੀ, ਜੋ ਕੋਰੋਨਾ ਵਾਇਰਸ ਦੇ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਬਾਅਦ ਲਾਕਡਾਊਨ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਸੀ। ਸਮਾਜੀ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਸਕ੍ਰਿਤਿਕ ਵਾਤਾਵਰਣ ਤੇਜ਼ੀ ਨਾਲ ਬਦਲ ਰਿਹਾ ਸੀ, ਜਿਸ ਕਾਰਨ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਰ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਖਾਸ ਮੌਕਾ ਸੀ। ਇਸ ਸਮੇਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੋਸਟ ਕੀਤੇ ਗਏ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਨੇ ਸਾਰੇ ਸਮੁੱਚੇ ਚਿੰਤਾਵਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਛੋਡਣ, ਜ਼ਰੂਰੀ ਮਜ਼ਾਕ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਨ ਜਾਂ ਸੰਕਟ ਦੇ ਵਿਸ਼ੇ ਤੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਬਾਹਰੀ ਰੂਪ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਵਨਾ ਰੱਖਦਾ ਸੀ।

ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਉਪਹਾਰ ਏ ਪੋਜੇ ਦੀ ਆਫ਼ੀਸ਼ਲ ਪੇਜ ਤੇ ਹੋਣ ਦੀ ਬਾਰੀ ਵੀ ਕੁਝ ਹੋਰ ਸੂਚਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਏ ਪੋਜੇ ਬ੍ਰਾਜ਼ੀਲੀਅਨ ਫੰਕ ਸੀਨ ਵਿੱਚ ਇੱਕ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਵਿਅਕਤੀ ਹੈ, ਇੱਕ ਗੀਤ ਜੋ ਆਪਣੇ ਅਸਲੀ ਕਮਿਊਨਿਟੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੁੜਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਹੈ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੀ ਆਪਣੀ ਕਿਸਮ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਗ੍ਰਾਹਕ ਸਮੂਹ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਦੀ ਲੋੜ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੀ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਰੁਚੀ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਮੁੱਖ ਗ੍ਰਾਹਕ ਸਮੂਹ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਹਰ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਵਿਆਪਕ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਉਪਭੋਗੀਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਹੋਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਸੀ, ਇਸ ਬਾਰੇ ਧਿਆਨ ਦੇਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਕਾਰਨਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਕੁਝ ਧਾਰਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੇ ਹਨ।

ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦਾ ਖਾਸ ਹੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ, ਪਰ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਮੂਲ ਉਪਹਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਪੋਸਟ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਤਰੀਕੇ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਕਿਸੇ ਵੀ ਸੂਚਨਾ ਨੂੰ ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਚਾਰਜ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰਗਟਾਵਾ ਦੀ ਸਮਝ ਲਈ ਮਹੱਤਵਪੂਰਨ ਸੂਚਨਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਸਮੇਂ ਏ ਪੋਜੇ ਦੀ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਉਪਲੱਬਧਤਾ ਦੀ ਜਾਂਚ ਅਤੇ ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦੇ ਹੱਲ ਦੀ ਵਿਸ਼ਲੇਸ਼ਣ ਕਰਨ ਵਾਲੇ ਕਾਰਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਦਦ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ, ਜੋ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਲੋਕਪ੍ਰਿਅਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਲੰਬੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਤੱਕ ਲੋਕਪ੍ਰਿਅਤਾ ਦੇ ਕਾਰਨਾਂ ਬਾਰੇ ਸੂਚਨਾ ਪ੍ਰਦਾਨ ਕਰ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ। ਵੀਡੀਓ ਦਾ ਮੂਲ ਸੋਸ਼ਲ ਮੀਡੀਆ ਪੋਸਟ ਤੋਂ ਇੱਕ ਵਾਇਰਲ ਘਟਨਾ ਵੱਲ ਬਦਲਣ ਦੀ ਯਾਤਰਾ ਆਨਲਾਈਨ ਵਾਇਰਲਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਦਰਭ ਦੀ ਮਹੱਤਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਸਮਝਣ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਦਿਲਚਸਪ ਅਧਿਐਨ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

## WHO Clarifies Statement on Asymptomatic COVID-19 Transmission

Confusion arose this week following comments made by Dr. Maria Van Kerkhove, the World Health Organization's (WHO) technical lead for the COVID-19 pandemic, regarding the transmission of the virus by asymptomatic individuals. During a press briefing on Monday, Dr. Van Kerkhove stated that COVID-19 transmission by asymptomatic patients appeared to be "rare." This statement sparked considerable debate and raised concerns about the potential impact on public health guidelines.

While her initial comment suggested a lower likelihood of asymptomatic spread, it's crucial to understand the nuances of her statement and the subsequent clarification issued by the WHO. Dr. Van Kerkhove did not imply that asymptomatic individuals pose no risk of transmission. Instead, her observation focused on the relative frequency of such occurrences.

Recognizing the potential for misinterpretation, the WHO quickly moved to clarify the matter. The organization emphasized that while asymptomatic transmission is less common than transmission from individuals exhibiting symptoms, it remains a distinct possibility. This clarification is significant because it reinforces the importance of ongoing preventative measures, such as mask-wearing, social distancing, and hand hygiene, regardless of whether individuals feel unwell.

The discussion around asymptomatic transmission highlights the complexities of understanding and controlling the COVID-19 pandemic. While more research is ongoing to determine the precise contribution of asymptomatic spread to overall transmission rates, the WHO's clarification underscores the need for continued vigilance and adherence to public health recommendations in order to mitigate the risk of infection. The ongoing evolution of scientific understanding necessitates careful communication and timely clarification to avoid confusion and maintain public trust in health guidance.

## WHO wyjaśnia stwierdzenie dotyczące przekazywania koronawirusa przez bezobjawowych

W tym tygodniu powstała niepewność po wydaniu przez dr. Marię Van Kerkhove, techniczną kierowniczkę Światowej Organizacji Zdrowia (WHO) w sprawach pandemii COVID-19, komentarzy dotyczących przekazywania wirusa przez osoby bezobjawowe. Podczas briefingu prasowego w poniedziałek dr. Van Kerkhove stwierdziła, że przekazywanie koronawirusa przez pacjentów bezobjawowych wydaje się "rzadkie". To stwierdzenie wywołało spore dyskusje i podniosło obawy co do potencjalnego wpływu na rekomendacje zdrowotne.

Choć jej początkowe stwierdzenie sugerowało niższy poziom ryzyka przekazywania się wirusem przez osoby bezobjawowe, ważne jest zrozumienie subtelności jej komentarza oraz subsekwentnej wyjaśnienia wydawanego przez WHO. Dr. Van Kerkhove nie sugerowała, że osoby bezobjawowe nie stanowią zagrożenia. Zamiast tego jej obserwacja skupiała się na względnej częstotliwości takich zdarzeń.

Uznając potencjalne nieporozumienie, WHO szybko podjęła działania w celu wyjaśnienia sytuacji. Organizacja podkreśliła, że choć przekazywanie się wirusem przez osoby bezobjawowe jest mniej powszechne niż przez osoby z objawami, nadal stanowi możliwe zjawisko. Ta wyjaśnienie jest istotna, ponieważ podkreśla znaczenie trwających mierze zapobiegawczych, takich jak noszenie masek, utrzymywanie dystansu społecznego i higiena rąk, niezależnie od tego, czy osoba czuje się dobrze, czy nie.

Dyskusja dotycząca przekazywania się wirusem przez osoby bezobjawowe podkreśla złożoność zrozumienia i kontroli pandemii COVID-19. Choć badania trwają, aby określić dokładny wkład przekazywania się wirusem przez bezobjawowych do ogólnych wskaźników zarażeń, wyjaśnienie WHO podkreśla konieczność ciągłego pilnowania i stosowania rekomendacji zdrowotnych w celu zmniejszenia ryzyka zarażenia. Trwały rozwój zrozumienia naukowego wymaga ostrożnego komunikowania się i szybkiej klarowności w celu uniknięcia niepewności i utrzymania zaufania do instrukcji zdrowotnych.

## Senate Amendment Mandates Mask Use in Public Spaces Across Brazil

A recent amendment to Bill 1562/2020, passed by the Federal Chamber on Tuesday (September 9th), establishes a mandatory mask policy for individuals in public and private spaces accessible to the public throughout Brazil. The amendment, introduced by the Senate, links this mandatory mask use to the duration of the state of public calamity declared due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

This decision signifies a significant step in the ongoing efforts to curb the spread of the novel coronavirus. While initially approved by the Federal Chamber, the Senate's addition clarifies and reinforces the existing, often inconsistent, guidelines regarding mask use nationwide. The bill’s initial passage through the Chamber suggests broad support for measures aimed at mitigating the health crisis.

The amendment specifies that the mandatory mask rule applies to "public and private spaces accessible to the public," a broad definition intended to encompass a wide range of locations. This likely includes, but is not limited to, streets, parks, public transportation, stores, restaurants, and other establishments that cater to the general public. By extending the mandate to both public and accessible private spaces, the Senate aims to minimize transmission risks in a variety of everyday settings.

The mandate's duration is explicitly tied to the state of public calamity declared in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. This means the mandatory mask requirement will remain in effect until the government deems the public health emergency over and formally revokes the state of calamity.

The specific enforcement mechanisms and potential penalties for non-compliance were not detailed in the initial announcement regarding the amendment's passage. Further clarification from governmental agencies is expected to outline the practical implementation of this new mandate and the consequences for individuals who fail to adhere to the rule. As the bill progresses through the legislative process, more information regarding enforcement and potential exemptions is anticipated. This amendment marks a key development in Brazil’s public health response to the ongoing pandemic.

## Senatov predlog obvezuje uporabo mask v javnih prostorih po vsej Braziliji

Nedavni predlog k законu 1562/2020, sprejeti v nedeljo (9. septembra) zbornico federalne skupine, določa obvezno uporabo mask pri osebah v javnih in zasebnih prostorih, dostopnih javnosti po vsej Braziliji. Predlog, predstavljen s strani Senata, povezuje to obvezno uporabo mask z trajanjem državnega stanja javne katastrofe zaradi pandemije COVID-19.

Ta odločitev predstavlja pomembni korak v trajnih naporih za zmanjšanje širjenja novega koronavirusa. Čeprav je bil predlog najprej sprejet zbornico federalne skupine, je Senatov dodatek jasno definiral in osiljal obstoječe, pogosto neenotne smernice glede uporabe mask po vsej državi. Prva prehod predloga skozi zbornico federalne skupine kaže na široko podporo ukrepom, namenjenim zmanjšanju zdravstvene krize.

Predlog določa, da obvezna uporaba mask velja za "javne in zasebne prostore, dostopne javnosti," široko definicijo, namenjeno vključevanju številne vrste lokacij. To vključuje, a ni omejeno na, ulice, parki, javno prevoz, trgovine, restavracije in druge ustanove, ki služijo javnosti. Z razširjanjem obveznosti na oba javne in dostopne zasebne prostore želi Senat zmanjšati tveganje za prenos v številnih vsakdanjih okoljih.

Trajanje obveznosti je jasno povezano z državnim stanjem javne katastrofe, ki je bilo izreceno zaradi pandemije COVID-19. To pomeni, da bo obvezna uporaba mask veljala do tedaj, ko bo vlada ocenila, da je javno zdravstveno varnostno stanje končano in formalno odpravila državno katastrofo.

Podrobnosti o izvajanju predloga in možnih sankcijah za neuskus v skladu z obveznostjo niso bile poudarjene v prvih objavah o sprejetju predloga. Nadaljnja pojasnila od strani vladnih organov so predvidena, da bodo opisala praktično izvajanje nove obveznosti in posledice za posameznike, ki ne sprostijo pravil. Ko bo predlog potekal skozi zakonodajni proces, so pričakovana dodatna informacije o izvajanju in možnih izpustkih. Ta predlog predstavlja ključen razvoj v Braziliji v odgovoru na trajno pandemijo.

## Woman Dies in Car Outside Mexico City Hospital, Photographer Captures Stark Reality of COVID-19 Triage

A stark image captured by photographer Moisés Pablo of the Cuartoscuro photo agency has highlighted the ongoing strain on Mexico City’s healthcare system amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The photograph, taken on Monday, August 8th, shows a somber scene unfolding in the parking lot of the Hospital General in the Mexican capital.

According to the caption accompanying the photograph on Cuartoscuro’s website, a woman died inside a vehicle while in the COVID-19 triage area of the hospital. The details remain sparse, but the image poignantly speaks to the pressures faced by hospitals and individuals alike navigating the complexities of the pandemic.

Cuartoscuro is a well-regarded photo agency in Mexico, known for its documentary and journalistic photography. Their work often captures the social and political realities of the country, providing a visual record of important events and issues. The inclusion of this photograph in their collection underscores the severity of the situation at the Hospital General and likely reflects similar scenes playing out at other medical facilities across Mexico City and beyond.

While the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death remain unclear, the fact that she passed away in her car within the triage area suggests a possible delay in receiving medical attention. This incident underscores the challenges healthcare systems worldwide have faced in managing patient flow, particularly during surges in COVID-19 cases. The pressure on resources, including staff, beds, and equipment, can lead to devastating outcomes for individuals seeking care.

This photograph serves as a powerful reminder of the human cost of the COVID-19 pandemic and the ongoing need to support healthcare workers and strengthen healthcare infrastructure. It also raises questions about access to timely medical care and the resources available to those seeking treatment for COVID-19 in Mexico City. The image, now circulating online, is prompting reflection and discussion about the pandemic's lasting impact on individuals and communities.

## COVID-19 Death Toll Dwarfs H1N1 Pandemic in First Six Months

Six months into the officially recognized COVID-19 pandemic, the global death toll has already surpassed the impact of the H1N1 influenza pandemic of 2009-2010 by a significant margin. As of June 12th, 2020, at least 418,294 people worldwide had died from COVID-19, according to confirmed cases. This figure highlights the stark difference in severity between the two respiratory illnesses, despite both being declared pandemics by the World Health Organization (WHO).

The WHO declared the H1N1 influenza, also known as swine flu, a pandemic in June of 2009. The pandemic lasted until August 2010. During this period, official figures documented 18,449 deaths attributed to H1N1 worldwide. **Police Officer in Amazonas Responds to Disinformation, Briefly Disrupts Hospital After Mistaking Video for Mother's Situation**

A police officer in Amazonas state briefly disrupted operations at a local hospital after acting on misinformation circulating on social media, believing his mother was about to be buried alive. The incident, which highlights the dangers of viral disinformation, occurred after the officer saw a video on WhatsApp depicting a woman, purportedly still alive, being placed inside a body bag.

The officer reportedly mistook the woman in the video for his mother, due in part to the similar dress being worn. Panic ensued as he believed his mother was the victim shown in the video, leading him to rush to the hospital.

Crucially, the video in question had already been debunked by fact-checkers. Its widespread circulation despite being proven false underscores the persistent challenge of combating misinformation, particularly on platforms like WhatsApp where content can spread rapidly within private groups, often without verification.

The incident serves as a stark reminder of the potential real-world consequences of online disinformation. While the officer's actions stemmed from understandable concern for his mother's well-being, they were directly influenced by a false narrative that had gained traction online. This case illustrates the need for increased media literacy and critical thinking skills within the population, as well as a greater emphasis on responsible information sharing to prevent similar incidents in the future. Authorities have not released further details on whether any disciplinary action will be taken against the officer. The hospital has also not commented on the disruption caused by the incident.

The specific type of hysterectomy performed, and the method used (abdominal, vaginal, or laparoscopic), depends on the patient's individual medical circumstances and the reason for the surgery.
