## कॉंग्रेस विधायक जोइस हासेलमैन मार्च में हिस्टेरेक्टोमी कराई

ब्राजील की कॉंग्रेस विधायक जोइस हासेलमैन (PSL-SP) मार्च 4 को एक हिस्टेरेक्टोमी नामक सर्जनी प्रक्रिया कराई गई, जिसमें गर्भाशय के अंग को हटाया जाता है। यह जानकारी पहले सोशल मीडिया पर घूम रही थी, जो निश्चित कर ली गई, हालांकि प्रक्रिया के विशिष्ट आंकड़े और उसके बाद उसकी बर्बादी के बारे में जानकारी बहुत कम है।

हिस्टेरेक्टोमी एक सामान्य सर्जनी प्रक्रिया है जो गर्भाशय के विभिन्न रोगों के इलाज के लिए की जाती है। इन रोगों में गर्भाशय के चक्राकार दुख, गर्भाशय के फाइब्रॉइड्स, एंडोमेट्रियोसिस, गर्भाशय के झुकाव, और कुछ मामलों में कुछ प्रकार के कैंसर शामिल हो सकते हैं। हिस्टेरेक्टोमी के विशिष्ट प्रकार और विधि (अभिविस्तार या वागीनल या लैपरोस्कोपिक) रोगी के व्यक्तिगत चिकित्सीय परिस्थितियों और सर्जरी के कारण पर निर्भर करती है।

हालांकि सोशल मीडिया पोस्ट में केवल प्रक्रिया की तारीख और सर्जरी के प्रकार का उल्लेख किया गया है, ऐसे चिकित्सीय निर्णय के प्रसंग को समझना महत्वपूर्ण है। हिस्टेरेक्टोमी एक महत्वपूर्ण सर्जरी है जो महिलाओं के जीवन को बदल सकती है, जिसका प्रभाव गर्भ धारण क्षमता और अगर गर्भाशय के साथ अंडाशय के हटाए जाने के कारण (ओफियोरेक्टोमी) हॉर्मोन स्तर पर भी पड़ सकता है।

एक पब्लिक आंकड़े के रूप में, हासेलमैन के स्वास्थ्य और विकास के बारे में उसके नागरिक और व्यापक सार्वजनिक रूप से रुचि रखते हैं। हालांकि, उसके व्यक्तिगत चिकित्सीय मामलों के संबंध में गोपनीयता के बारे में भी बर्बादी बर्दाश्त करना आवश्यक है। उसके हिस्टेरेक्टोमी के कारण और उसकी बर्बादी के विशिष्ट आंकड़े के बारे में अधिक जानकारी नहीं दी गई है, और कोई अनुमान बर्बादी करना बर्बादी है।

अब ध्यान उसकी बर्बादी और उसकी कॉंग्रेस में अपने नागरिकों के लिए सेवा करने की क्षमता पर है। उसके पेशेवर गतिविधियों के बारे में आगे के अपडेट आने की उम्मीद है।

## CoronaVac Vaccine Trials in China Showed Promise in Early Stages

Early clinical trials of the CoronaVac vaccine, developed by the Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac Biotech, involved hundreds of volunteers in China and provided initial data on its safety and efficacy. The trials, conducted in two distinct phases, focused on assessing the vaccine's performance in a relatively narrow age range.

The initial phase 1 trial enrolled 143 adult volunteers. Typically, Phase 1 trials are primarily designed to evaluate the safety profile of a vaccine candidate. Researchers closely monitor participants for any adverse reactions and begin to determine the appropriate dosage. This initial stage is crucial for identifying potential red flags before progressing to larger and more complex trials.

Building on the findings of Phase 1, the subsequent Phase 2 trial involved a significantly larger cohort of 600 volunteers. This phase not only continued to monitor safety but also began to gather data on the vaccine's immunogenicity, meaning its ability to stimulate an immune response within the body. Researchers would have assessed the levels of antibodies produced in response to the vaccine, indicating whether the body was learning to recognize and fight the virus.

Both phases specifically recruited individuals between the ages of 18 and 59. This age range suggests that the initial research focused on the segment of the population generally considered to be at lower risk of severe COVID-19 complications than older adults. The decision to focus on this age group likely allowed researchers to efficiently gather initial data on safety and immunogenicity before expanding trials to include older populations, which often require more careful monitoring.

It is important to note that these were early-stage trials. Further and larger-scale Phase 3 trials, typically conducted across multiple countries and involving thousands of participants, are necessary to fully evaluate the vaccine's efficacy against COVID-19 in real-world conditions and across diverse populations. These later trials would also provide a more comprehensive understanding of the vaccine's safety profile and long-term effects. While the initial Chinese trials provided valuable groundwork, the widespread adoption and global impact of CoronaVac ultimately hinged on the results of these subsequent, more extensive studies.

## Chinese Investment in Global Brands: A Pre-Pandemic Trend

A recent social media post highlighted the acquisition of stakes, or complete buyouts, of several prominent European brands – Volvo, Pirelli, Thomas Cook, and Mercedes-Benz – by Chinese companies. While the observation itself is noteworthy, the timing of these transactions is crucial: all of the deals in question were finalized before the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic.

This detail places these acquisitions within the context of a broader trend of increasing Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI) in global brands, particularly in the automotive and travel sectors. Prior to the pandemic, Chinese companies were actively seeking opportunities to expand their reach and gain access to established technologies, distribution networks, and brand recognition, which these established Western companies offered.

Volvo, the Swedish car manufacturer, was acquired by Geely Holding Group in 2010. This purchase provided Geely with access to Volvo’s advanced engineering and safety technology, allowing them to significantly improve the quality and appeal of their own domestic brand.

Similarly, Pirelli, the renowned Italian tire manufacturer, saw ChemChina acquire a majority stake in 2015. This move provided ChemChina, a state-owned chemical company, with access to Pirelli’s expertise in tire technology and global supply chains, strengthening its position in the global tire market.

The case of Thomas Cook, the British travel agency, is slightly different. While Fosun International acquired the travel agency's brand and hotel assets following its collapse in 2019, this happened after the company had already declared bankruptcy, and represents a rescue operation rather than a straightforward acquisition.

While Mercedes-Benz wasn't fully acquired, in 2018, Geely bought a significant 9.69% stake in Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, becoming the largest single shareholder. This move gave Geely a significant foothold in the luxury car market and access to Daimler's technology and innovation.

The pre-pandemic timeline is important because the global economic landscape has dramatically shifted since the start of 2020. The pandemic's impact on global trade, supply chains, and investment flows has undoubtedly altered the dynamics of cross-border acquisitions. Whether this trend of Chinese investment in global brands will continue at the same pace remains to be seen, but the aforementioned deals serve as a significant example of the pre-pandemic landscape.

## Inversió china en marques globals: una tendència pre-pandèmica

Una publicació recent a les xarxes socials va destacar l'adquisició d'accions, o compravendes completes, de diverses marques europees destacades – Volvo, Pirelli, Thomas Cook i Mercedes-Benz – per part d'empreses xineses. Encara que l'observació en si mateixa és significativa, el moment d'aquestes operacions és crucial: tots els acords mencionats es van finalitzar abans de l'inici de la pandèmia de COVID-19.

Aquest detall col·loca aquestes adquisicions dins del context d'una tendència més ampla d'increment de l'inversió directa estrangera (IDE) de la Xina en marques globals, especialment en sectors com el vehicle i el turisme. Abans de la pandèmia, les empreses xineses estaven activament buscant oportunitats per ampliar la seva presència i accedir a tecnologies establertes, xarxes de distribució i reconeixement de marca, que aquestes companyies occidentals ja tenien.

Volvo, l'empresa de cotxes sueca, va ser adquirida per la Geely Holding Group el 2010. Aquesta compra va permetre a la Geely accedir a l'enginyeria i la tecnologia de seguretat avançada de Volvo, permetent-li millorar significativament la qualitat i l'apel·lació de la seva pròpia marca domèstica.

De manera similar, Pirelli, la coneguda empresa italiana de pneumàtics, va veure com la ChemChina adquiria una participació majoritària el 2015. Aquest moviment va permetre a la ChemChina, una empresa química estatal, accedir a la competència en tecnologia de pneumàtics i xarxes de distribució globals, fortaleixent la seva posició en el mercat mundial dels pneumàtics.

El cas de Thomas Cook, l'agència de viatges britànica, és lleugerament diferent. Tot i que Fosun International va adquirir la marca i els actius d'hotel dels serveis de viatge després de la seva quiebra el 2019, això va succeir després que l'empresa hagués declarat la quiebra, i representa una operació de rescatar, no una adquisició directa.

Tot i que Mercedes-Benz no va ser adquirida de forma total, el 2018 la Geely va comprar una participació significativa del 9,69% a Daimler, la companyia mare de Mercedes-Benz, convertint-se en l'accionista més gran individual. Aquest moviment va donar a la Geely una presència important en el mercat de cotxes de luxe i l'acces a la tecnologia i innovació de Daimler.

El moment pre-pandèmica és important, ja que el marc econòmic global s'ha modificat dràsticament des del començament del 2020. L'impacte de la pandèmia en el comerç mundial, les xarxes de subministrament i els fluxos d'inversió ha segurament canviat les dinàmiques de les adquisicions transfrontereres. Què passarà amb aquesta tendència d'inversió china en marques globals, si continuarà a la mateixa velocitat, encara és incert, però les operacions mencionades són un exemple significatiu del context pre-pandèmic.

## WHO Clarifies CoronaVac Testing Procedures Amid Disinformation

Recent social media posts have falsely claimed that the World Health Organization (WHO) admitted that the CoronaVac vaccine, developed by Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac, was not tested in any country. This claim is inaccurate and misrepresents the WHO's evaluation and endorsement process for vaccines, including CoronaVac.

The WHO grants Emergency Use Listing (EUL) to vaccines that meet rigorous quality, safety, and efficacy standards. This listing allows countries to expedite their own regulatory approvals to import and administer these vaccines, particularly during public health emergencies like the COVID-19 pandemic. To receive EUL, vaccines must undergo extensive testing, including clinical trials conducted in diverse populations across various geographical locations.

In the case of CoronaVac, the WHO meticulously reviewed data from clinical trials conducted in multiple countries, including Brazil, Indonesia, Turkey, and Chile. These trials involved tens of thousands of participants and demonstrated that CoronaVac met the WHO's efficacy threshold of at least 50% against symptomatic COVID-19 disease. The WHO's independent advisory group, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), further assessed the available evidence and recommended the vaccine's use.

The assertion that CoronaVac wasn't tested in any country directly contradicts the publicly available information on the WHO's website and in scientific publications. The WHO’s assessment process relies heavily on clinical trial data generated across different geographic regions and demographic groups to ensure the vaccine's suitability for global use.

Misinformation surrounding vaccines can erode public trust and hinder vaccination efforts, ultimately prolonging the pandemic and endangering lives. It is crucial to rely on credible sources, such as the WHO and national health authorities, for accurate information about vaccine safety and efficacy. Before sharing information related to the COVID-19 pandemic, fact-checking and verifying information from reliable sources is a must. Disseminating inaccurate claims about vaccines undermines public health and contributes to confusion at a time when clear, evidence-based information is most needed.

Bu iddia yanlış ve WHO'nun aşılar, Koronavak dahil olmak üzere, etkinlik ve güvenilirlik kriterlerine uygun olduğunda değerlendirmesini ve onayını temsil etmez.

WHO, kalite, güvenlik ve etkinlik standartlarını karşılayan aşıları Acil Kullanım Listesi (EUL) ile onaylar. Bu listeye dahil edilen aşılar, özellikle pandemiler gibi kamu sağlığı krizlerinde, ülkelerin kendi düzenleyici onay süreçlerini hızlandırarak bu aşıları ithal etmelerine ve uygulamalarına olanak tanır. EUL almak isteyen aşılar, farklı coğrafi bölgelerde ve demografik gruplarda yapılan geniş çaplı testlerden geçmelidir.

Koronavak durumunda, WHO, Brezilya, Endonezya, Türkiye ve Çile gibi birçok ülkede yapılan klinik deneylerin verilerini dikkatlice incelemiştir. Bu deneyler on binlerce katılımcıya ulaşmış ve Koronavak'ın en az %50 etkinlik eşiğini karşıladığını göstermiştir. Koronavak'ın hiçbir ülde test edilmediğini iddia eden ifade, WHO'nun web sitesinde ve bilimsel yayınlarla kamuoyuna açık bilgilerle doğrudan çelişir. Aşılarla ilgili yanlış bilgiler, halk güvenini zedeler ve aşılama çabalarını engeller, bu da pandeminin uzamasına ve can kaybına neden olur. Aşı güvenliği ve etkinliği hakkında doğru bilgi için WHO ve ulusal sağlık kurumları gibi güvenilir kaynaklara güvenmek önemlidir. Koronavak-19 pandemisiyle ilgili bilgileri paylaşmadan önce bilgiyi doğrulamak ve güvenilir kaynaklardan doğrulamak zorunludur. Aşılarla ilgili yanlış iddialar, halk sağlığına zarar verir ve kanıtlanmış bilgiye olan ihtiyacı artıran bir zamanda kargaşaya neden olur.

## Viral Image Misidentified as COVID-19 Symptom, Actually Shows Strep Infection

A photo circulating online, widely shared and often misattributed to COVID-19, actually depicts a symptom of a bacterial infection caused by Streptococcus bacteria, according to fact-checking efforts. The image, which has been used in numerous social media posts to illustrate the potential health impacts of the coronavirus, has been definitively linked to a different illness entirely.

The spread of the misinformation highlights a growing problem: the misrepresentation of medical imagery and information online, particularly in the context of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. The original source of the image and the specific context in which it was initially published are currently being investigated. However, the consensus among medical professionals and fact-checking organizations is that it is not related to COVID-19.

The sharing of inaccurate medical information, even with good intentions, can have serious consequences. It can lead to unnecessary panic and anxiety, as well as potentially influence individuals to make uninformed decisions regarding their health and safety.

This incident serves as a critical reminder to carefully vet the information we consume and share online. It’s crucial to rely on reputable sources of medical information, such as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the World Health Organization (WHO), and trusted medical professionals. Before sharing a health-related image or claim, it's advisable to conduct a thorough search to verify its accuracy and context, especially when related to sensitive topics like viral outbreaks and potential symptoms. The responsible sharing of information is crucial in preventing the spread of misinformation and protecting public health.

**False Attributions: Viral Text Misattributed to C.S. Lewis Circulates Online**

A text passage widely shared on social media platforms, often attributed to C.S. Lewis and purportedly taken from his famed work "The Screwtape Letters" (Spanish title: "Cartas del Diablo a su Sobrino"), is falsely attributed. This has prompted fact-checking organizations and literary scholars to issue clarifications regarding its true origin.

"The Screwtape Letters," a satirical epistolary novel published in 1942, presents a series of letters from a senior demon, Screwtape, to his nephew Wormwood, a junior tempter, offering guidance on how to corrupt a human soul. The book's insightful exploration of temptation, faith, and human nature has made it a perennial favorite and a source of numerous quotations.

However, the specific passage in question, which has gained significant traction on social media, does *not* appear within the actual text of "The Screwtape Letters." While the content of the misattributed passage may align thematically with some of the book’s broader concepts about spiritual warfare, it is essential to recognize that C.S. Lewis did not author it.

The proliferation of this false attribution highlights the dangers of relying solely on social media for information, especially when dealing with matters of authorship and attribution. In the age of rapid information sharing, misinformation can spread quickly and widely, creating confusion and distorting the historical record.

Readers and social media users are encouraged to verify the authenticity of quotations before sharing them, particularly when attributed to well-known authors. Checking reputable sources, such as published editions of the book, scholarly articles, or fact-checking websites, can help prevent the spread of inaccurate information and ensure that authors receive proper credit for their work. The accurate attribution of quotes is crucial to maintaining intellectual honesty and respecting the legacy of literary figures like C.S. Lewis.

## Fact Check: São Paulo Governor Doria Did Not Propose Testing CoronaVac on Elderly Brazilians

Recent social media posts have falsely claimed that São Paulo Governor João Doria (PSDB) proposed testing the CoronaVac vaccine, developed by the Chinese pharmaceutical company Sinovac, specifically on elderly individuals in Brazil. This claim, however, has been debunked after a thorough review of Governor Doria's public statements and available reports on the vaccine's clinical trials.

An examination of press conferences given by the governor, as well as news coverage of the CoronaVac clinical trials in Brazil, has yielded no evidence to support the allegation. No documented instance exists where Doria explicitly proposed or even implied that the vaccine should be tested exclusively or primarily on elderly Brazilians.

Furthermore, Governor Doria's press office has explicitly refuted the claim, stating that the information circulating on social media is false. This denial underscores the lack of factual basis for the accusation.

The CoronaVac vaccine, during its clinical trials in Brazil, was tested on a broad range of adult volunteers, including healthcare professionals, who were considered high-risk individuals due to their exposure to COVID-19. While the elderly population is a vulnerable group that benefited from the vaccine's subsequent approval and distribution, the initial clinical trials were not specifically targeted towards this demographic.

The spread of misinformation regarding COVID-19 vaccines remains a significant concern, especially considering the potential impact on public health. It is crucial to verify the accuracy of information before sharing it online and to rely on credible sources, such as official government statements, reputable news organizations, and scientific publications. The debunking of this particular claim highlights the importance of critical analysis and fact-checking in navigating the complex information landscape surrounding the pandemic.

## ତାରତମ୍ୟ: ସାଓ ପାଉଲୋ ମୁଖ୍ୟମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଡୋରିଆ ବ୍ରାଜିଲୀୟନ ପ୍ରାଚୀର ବୟସ୍କମାନଙ୍କ ଉପରେ କୋରୋନାଭାକ୍ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ ପ୍ରପୋନ୍ କରିନଥିଲେ

ପ୍ରାଚୀର ସାମାଜିକ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ହୋଇଥିବା ବିଷୟରେ ମିଥ୍ୟା ଦାବି କରାଯାଇଛି ଯେ ସାଓ ପାଉଲୋ ମୁଖ୍ୟମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଜୋଇଅସ୍ ଡୋରିଆ (ପିଏସ୍ଡିବି) ଚୀନୀ ଔଷଧ କମ୍ପାନୀ ସିନୋଭାକ୍ ଦ୍ୱାରା ନିର୍ମାଣ କରାଯାଇଥିବା କୋରୋନାଭାକ୍ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍କୁ ବ୍ରାଜିଲୀୟନ ପ୍ରାଚୀର ବୟସ୍କମାନଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ କରିବାର ପ୍ରପୋନ୍ କରିଥିଲେ। ଏହି ଦାବି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ହୋଇଛି କାରଣ ମୁଖ୍ୟମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଡୋରିଆଙ୍କ ପ୍ରାବନ୍ଧନ ଓ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ ଉପରେ ଉପଲବ୍ଧ ରିପୋର୍ଟ୍ରୁ ଗବେଷଣା କରା ପରେ।

ମୁଖ୍ୟମନ୍ତ୍ରୀଙ୍କ ପ୍ରାବନ୍ଧନରେ ପ୍ରଦାନ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ପତ୍ରିକାର ବିବରଣୀ ଏବଂ ବ୍ରାଜିଲ୍ରେ କୋରୋନାଭାକ୍ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣର ପତ୍ରିକା ବିବରଣୀରେ ଏହି ଦାବିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମିଳିନାହିଁ। କୌଣସି ରେକର୍ଡ୍ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ଘଟଣା ମଧ୍ୟ ନାହିଁ ଯେ ଡୋରିଆ ପ୍ରାଚୀର ବୟସ୍କମାନଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ବା ପ୍ରାଥମିକ ଭାବରେ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ପ୍ରପୋନ୍ କରିଥିଲେ ବା ଅଭିହିତ କରିଥିଲେ।

ଅଧିକଂଶ ଭାବରେ, ମୁଖ୍ୟମନ୍ତ୍ରୀ ଡୋରିଆଙ୍କ ପ୍ରେସ୍ ଅଫିସ୍ ଏହି ଦାବିକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରିଛି ଯେ ସାମାଜିକ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ହୋଇଥିବା ତଥ୍ୟ ମିଥ୍ୟା। ଏହି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରିବା ଅପେକ୍ଷାକୃତ ଦାବିର କୌଣସି ତଥ୍ୟପୂର୍ବକ ଭିତ୍ତି ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରିଛି।

କୋରୋନାଭାକ୍ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ର ବ୍ରାଜିଲ୍ରେ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ ସମୟରେ, ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍କୁ ବ୍ୟାପକ ବୟସ୍କ ପ୍ରାଣୀଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା, ଯାହାରେ ଚିକିତ୍ସା କର୍ମୀମାନେ ଅନ୍ତର୍ଭୁକ୍ତ ଥିଲେ, ଯାହାମାନେ କରୋନାଭାଇରସ୍ ପ୍ରତି ପ୍ରତିରୋଧରେ ଅଧିକ ବିପଦମୁକ୍ତ ବୋଲି ବିବେଚନା କରାଯାଇଥିଲା। ଯାହାଙ୍କର ବୟସ୍କ ଜନତା ବିପଦମୁକ୍ତ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ ଏବଂ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ର ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପ୍ରବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଓ ବିତରଣ ପରେ ଅନ୍ତର୍ଭୁକ୍ତ ହୋଇଥିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରାରମ୍ଭିକ ପରୀକ୍ଷଣ ଏହି ଜନତାକୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କରାଯାଇଥିଲା ନାହିଁ।

କୋରୋନାଭାଇରସ୍ ଭାକ୍ସିନ୍ ବିଷୟରେ ଅପରିଚିତ ତଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରସାର ପ୍ରାଚୀର ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ ଉପରେ ଅଧିକ ପ୍ରଭାବ ପାଇପାରେ, ଏହା ଏକ ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ହୋଇଛି। ଆଇନ୍ତର୍ଜାତୀୟ ମାଧ୍ୟମରେ ତଥ୍ୟ ପ୍ରସାର କରିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ତଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ହେବା ଆବଶ୍ୟକ। ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ଏହି ଦାବି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରିଛି ଯେ ମହାମାରୀ ବିଷୟରେ ଜଟିଳ ତଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରବାହରେ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କରିବା ଓ ତଥ୍ୟଚକ୍ରରେ କ୍ରିତିକ ବିଶ୍ଳେଷଣ ଓ ତଥ୍ୟପରୀକ୍ଷଣ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ହୋଇଛି।

**Viral Video From Tel Aviv Hospital Misinterpreted as COVID-19 Celebration**

A video recently circulating online, purporting to show medical staff at the Sourasky Medical Center in Tel Aviv, Israel, celebrating the end of COVID-19 patients within their unit, has been widely misinterpreted. The video, which was originally posted on the hospital’s Facebook page on April 6th, has been taken out of context, leading to the erroneous conclusion.

Contrary to the claims accompanying the video, the footage does not depict a celebration related to the absence of COVID-19 patients. Instead, the hospital has clarified that the video was recorded shortly before the start of Passover, or Pesach, the Jewish holiday commemorating the liberation of the ancient Israelites from slavery in Egypt.

Passover is a significant religious and cultural event marked by festive meals, rituals, and traditions. It is a time for families and communities to come together and celebrate freedom. It is common for organizations, including hospitals, to mark the upcoming holiday with events to boost morale and camaraderie.

The original context of the video, therefore, was to showcase the hospital staff preparing for and celebrating Passover, a time of joy and liberation. The misinterpretation highlights the ease with which information can be spread online without proper verification, leading to the circulation of inaccurate narratives. The Sourasky Medical Center's clarification aims to set the record straight and ensure that the video is understood in its intended context – a pre-Passover celebration amongst dedicated healthcare professionals.

**Health Ministry Denies Funneling Funds Based on COVID-19 Death Toll**

The Ministry of Health has issued a statement clarifying its funding allocation practices during the COVID-19 pandemic, explicitly denying that funds are transferred to states and municipalities based on the number of registered COVID-19 deaths. The clarification comes amid concerns about potential incentives for inflating death tolls or perceived inequities in resource distribution.

In the statement, the Ministry underscored that resource allocation for combating the pandemic is determined proportionally to the population size of each state. This means that states with larger populations receive a greater share of the allocated funds, regardless of their COVID-19 mortality figures.

This approach aims to ensure that resources are distributed based on the overall healthcare needs of each region, acknowledging that larger populations generally require more resources to manage various aspects of the pandemic response, including testing, treatment, vaccination campaigns, and public health initiatives.

The Ministry's statement attempts to address potential anxieties surrounding the fairness and transparency of funding distribution. By clarifying that death tolls are not a factor in allocation decisions, the Ministry seeks to reassure the public that the allocation process is objective and focused on serving the healthcare needs of all citizens. This transparency is crucial for maintaining public trust in the government's handling of the ongoing health crisis. It remains to be seen if this statement will fully address existing concerns among local governments and citizens. The Ministry will likely need to continue to communicate its funding policies clearly and openly to ensure accountability and public confidence.

## Video Misattributed: Celebration of Declining COVID Cases Occurred at Fortaleza Emergency Care Unit, Not Hospital

A video circulating online, initially claimed to be filmed within the Dr. Carlos Alberto Studart Gomes Hospital in Messejana, actually depicts a celebration at a different healthcare facility. According to information provided by the press office of the Emergency Care Unit (UPA) in a Fortaleza neighborhood, the video was filmed on June 17th and shows staff celebrating a significant reduction in the number of COVID-19 patients.

The UPA, which operates under the purview of the Ceará State Health Secretariat, confirmed via telephone that the footage captured a moment of relief and optimism amongst healthcare workers on the front lines of the pandemic. The initial misattribution of the video highlights the continued sensitivity surrounding COVID-19 and the pressure faced by healthcare systems during the pandemic.

While the video's precise content and context are still developing, the UPA's confirmation provides crucial clarity. The video, regardless of its location, speaks to the emotional toll of the pandemic on medical professionals who have tirelessly worked to combat the virus. The decrease in COVID-19 patients would understandably be a welcome development, providing much-needed respite and potentially signaling a turning point in the local fight against the virus.

The incident also underscores the importance of verifying information shared on social media, particularly when dealing with sensitive topics related to health and public safety. Misinformation can quickly spread, leading to confusion and potentially damaging the reputation of institutions and individuals. This case serves as a reminder to critically evaluate sources and seek confirmation from official channels before sharing potentially inaccurate information online. The Ceará State Health Secretariat and associated UPAs continue to play a vital role in providing accessible healthcare throughout the region, as they continue to manage the ongoing situation.

**Brazilian Navy Clarifies Controversial Document, Asserts Proposed Measures Were Not Adopted**

Brasilia – A document circulating online that detailed potential measures or procedures within the Brazilian Navy has been clarified by the institution's press office. According to an official statement, the circulated document was merely a "draft protocol" and was never formally adopted by the Brazilian Navy.

The statement, issued by the Navy's press office, seeks to quell speculation and potential misinformation stemming from the dissemination of the protocol draft. The distinction between a draft and an official document is crucial. While drafts represent potential strategies, procedures, or guidelines under consideration, they are not binding or operational until formally approved and implemented.

The Navy's clarification emphasizes that the measures outlined in the leaked draft remained proposals and were not put into practice. The press office's deliberate choice of words highlights the internal review process within the military institution. Before any new procedure or protocol is implemented, it typically undergoes a series of reviews, revisions, and approvals. This rigorous process aims to ensure the measures align with existing regulations, operational standards, and overall strategic objectives of the Navy.

The Navy's response underscores the importance of verifying information, particularly in the age of rapid information sharing through social media and online platforms. The potential for misinterpretation and the spread of inaccurate information necessitates clear and timely communication from official sources. By issuing a statement, the Brazilian Navy sought to preempt any further confusion or misrepresentation of the document's significance, reaffirming that it was simply a proposal that was never implemented. Further details regarding the specific content of the draft protocol have not been released by the Brazilian Navy.

## Claim Attributed to Donald Trump Found to Be Unsubstantiated

A recent claim attributed to former US President Donald Trump has been found to be unsubstantiated after a thorough review of official records and public statements. The claim, circulating widely online, features a quote attributed to Trump, allegedly captured as an epigraph on an image. However, investigation reveals no evidence to support the claim that Trump ever made the statement.

A search of Trump's official Twitter account, the platform he frequently used to communicate during his presidency, found no record of the purported quote. The account, a primary source for tracking his public statements, contains no mention of the phrase or anything resembling its sentiment. The absence of the quote on his official Twitter feed raises serious doubts about its authenticity, given the platform's historical use for immediate and widespread communication.

Further investigation involved a comprehensive search of news archives and media databases. Multiple searches using keywords related to the attributed quote, along with variations and potential paraphrases, yielded no results. This lack of media coverage surrounding the supposed statement further casts doubt on its veracity. Had such a statement been made by a figure as prominent as the former President, it is highly probable that it would have been reported by news outlets.

The absence of both official record and media coverage strongly suggests that the attributed quote is false. In an era of increased online misinformation, it is crucial to verify the authenticity of claims, especially those attributed to prominent figures. The spread of unsubstantiated claims can contribute to confusion and distrust in public discourse. This instance underscores the importance of critical thinking and thorough fact-checking before sharing information online. Users are encouraged to consult reliable sources and verify information before amplifying potentially false claims.

Recent social media posts suggesting that San Paulo Mayor Bruno Covas (PSDB) stated he used chloroquine in his COVID-19 treatment during a CNN interview have been refuted. Several health organizations, including the World Health Organization and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, have cautioned against its widespread use outside of clinical trials.

The spread of misinformation regarding Mayor Covas's supposed endorsement of chloroquine highlights the challenges of navigating the complex and often politicized landscape of COVID-19 treatment information. ## Supreme Court Upholds State and Local Autonomy in Brazil's COVID-19 Response

Brasilia - The Supreme Federal Court (STF), Brazil's highest court, has ruled that state governors and mayors possess the autonomy to implement their own strategies in combating the COVID-19 pandemic within their respective jurisdictions. The decision, stemming from three separate legal actions brought before the court, clarifies the division of powers in Brazil's response to the ongoing health crisis.

Contrary to some initial interpretations, the STF's ruling did not remove President Jair Bolsonaro from overseeing national strategic measures related to the pandemic. Instead, the court affirmed the long-established principle of federalism, granting subnational entities the authority to tailor their approaches to the specific needs and circumstances of their communities.

The legal challenges brought before the STF sought clarity on the extent of federal versus state and local powers in enacting measures to contain the spread of the virus. The court's decision clarifies that while the federal government retains the authority to implement national-level policies, state governors and mayors have the independent power to establish local regulations, including measures such as business closures, social distancing protocols, and mandatory mask mandates.

This ruling reinforces the ability of state and local governments to respond effectively to localized outbreaks and implement strategies deemed most appropriate for their populations. The decision acknowledges the diverse realities across Brazil's vast geography and varying population densities, allowing for a more nuanced and localized approach to pandemic management.

The STF's verdict effectively distributes responsibility for pandemic control across different levels of government, potentially leading to a more comprehensive and responsive strategy overall. While the federal government can continue to set national guidelines and provide resources, the autonomy granted to states and municipalities enables them to adapt and implement specific measures tailored to their unique needs and challenges. The implications of this decision will likely be seen in varying approaches to managing the pandemic across different regions of Brazil.

The note explicitly states that the promotion is being conducted "by a third party that uses [the Xiaomi brand] without our authorization." This declaration aims to prevent consumers from being misled into participating in a potentially fraudulent or deceptive campaign.

While the specific details of the promotion were not outlined in the statement, the explicit denial suggests that Xiaomi Brazil is aware of unauthorized marketing activities leveraging their brand name. This type of situation is not uncommon in the increasingly complex digital landscape, where brands often face the challenge of monitoring and combating unauthorized use of their intellectual property for promotional purposes.

## Doctor Who Championed Hydroxychloroquine Leaves Hospital in Bahia

Dr. Raissa Soares, a physician who gained significant social media attention for her advocacy of hydroxychloroquine as a treatment for COVID-19, has left her position at the Hospital Regional Diputado Luís Eduardo Magalhães (HRDLEM) in Porto Seguro, Bahia. However, contrary to some speculation online, Dr. Soares was not dismissed from her post.

According to both Dr. Soares herself and the hospital's management, the decision for her to leave the HRDLEM stemmed from conflicting professional commitments. Dr. Soares stated that other professional obligations were making it difficult for her to fulfill her scheduled shifts at the regional hospital. This explanation was confirmed by HRDLEM administration, who denied any termination was involved.

Dr. Soares’ departure marks the end of a period where she was a highly visible figure, particularly online, advocating for the use of hydroxychloroquine in treating COVID-19. This stance, controversial since the early stages of the pandemic, generated significant public discussion and positioned her as a key proponent of the drug within Brazil's online landscape.

While the effectiveness of hydroxychloroquine against COVID-19 has been widely refuted by scientific consensus and major health organizations globally, it remained a topic of heated debate in certain circles, including some political spheres in Brazil. Dr. Soares' vocal support, shared and amplified through social media, contributed to this continued discussion, regardless of medical and scientific advice.

The hospital's confirmation that the departure was due to scheduling conflicts aims to dispel any rumors that may have arisen about her leaving due to her controversial medical views. It underscores that the decision was a practical one, based on her ability to meet the demands of her work schedule alongside other professional engagements.

Доктор Соарес заявила, что другие профессиональные обязательства затрудняют её выполнение графика работы в региональной больнице. Это объяснение подтвердил административный персонал HRDLEM, который отверг любой упоминания об увольнении.

Подтверждение больницы, что уход доктора Соарес связан с конфликтами графика, направлено на развеивание слухов, возникших из-за её спорной позиции в медицине. Recent online activity highlights a critical issue in the digital age: the spread of misinformation. A circulating text on social media is causing concern by incorrectly conflating separate reports regarding different viruses affecting swine populations. While both reports are genuine, their amalgamation in this single post creates an alarmist narrative unsupported by factual evidence.

The crux of the problem lies in the misinterpretation and merging of distinct news items. It appears users are combining information about two different viruses, each with its own characteristics, geographical location, and impact on swine. Without proper understanding, this blending of information can lead to inaccurate conclusions about the potential threat to both animal health and potentially, the food supply.

Authorities in the agricultural and veterinary sectors are aware of the need to combat this type of misinformation. These institutions rely on verified scientific data and rigorous research to track and manage animal diseases. They regularly issue statements and updates to keep farmers, industry professionals, and the public informed about the actual risks and preventative measures.

The ease with which information, and misinformation, can spread on social media underscores the importance of critical thinking and responsible sharing. Before amplifying potentially alarming reports, individuals should verify the source and seek information from reputable organizations like governmental agricultural agencies, veterinary associations, and peer-reviewed scientific publications. These sources provide accurate and contextualized information, helping to separate genuine threats from exaggerated or fabricated narratives. In this case, a healthy dose of skepticism and a commitment to reliable sources can effectively counter the spread of panic fuelled by online misinformation regarding swine viruses.

## WHO Debunks Claims of Garlic as COVID-19 Cure

The World Health Organization (WHO) has publicly addressed a circulating myth regarding garlic's potential to combat the novel coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. In a statement published on its website, the WHO acknowledged garlic's known antimicrobial properties but explicitly stated that there is no scientific evidence to support its efficacy in preventing or curing the disease.

The statement aims to counter the spread of misinformation surrounding alternative treatments for COVID-19. In the wake of the pandemic, various unproven remedies have surfaced online and within communities, often fueled by anecdotal evidence and a desire for readily available solutions. Garlic, a common kitchen staple known for its potential health benefits, has been among the substances promoted as a preventative or curative measure against the virus.

While garlic contains compounds, like allicin, that have demonstrated antimicrobial effects in laboratory settings, these findings do not translate into a proven treatment for a specific viral infection like COVID-19 within the human body. The concentration of these compounds required to achieve a significant antiviral effect is often far greater than what can be realistically consumed through dietary intake. Furthermore, the complex mechanisms of viral infections necessitate targeted medical interventions, not just broad antimicrobial agents.

The WHO's clarification emphasizes the importance of relying on evidence-based medicine and consulting with healthcare professionals for accurate information about preventing and treating COVID-19. While a healthy diet, including garlic, can contribute to overall well-being and a strong immune system, it should not be considered a substitute for proven preventative measures such as vaccination, mask-wearing, and social distancing, or for established medical treatments prescribed by qualified healthcare providers. The organization continues to urge the public to be vigilant against misinformation and to seek credible sources of information during the ongoing pandemic.

## L'OMS Smentisce le Affermazioni sullo Spicchio d'Aglio come Guarigione dal Coronavirus

L'Organizzazione Mondiale della Sanità (OMS) ha pubblicamente smentito un mito circolante riguardo al potenziale dell'aglio nel combattere il nuovo coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, il virus responsabile del COVID-19. In una dichiarazione pubblicata sul suo sito web, l'OMS ha riconosciuto le proprietà antimicrobiche note dell'aglio, ma ha esplicitamente affermato che non esiste alcuna prova scientifica a supporto della sua efficacia nel prevenire o curare la malattia.

La dichiarazione mira a contrastare la diffusione di informazioni errate riguardo alle terapie alternative per il COVID-19. Nella fase della pandemia, sono emersi vari rimedi non provati online e all'interno delle comunità, spesso alimentati da evidenze anecdotiche e dalla ricerca di soluzioni facilmente reperibili. L'aglio, un prodotto comune della cucina noto per i suoi possibili benefici per la salute, è stato tra le sostanze promosse come misura preventiva o curativa contro il virus.

Sebbene l'aglio contenga composti, come l'allicina, che hanno dimostrato effetti antimicrobici in ambienti di laboratorio, tali scoperte non si traducono in un trattamento provato per un'infezione virale specifica come il COVID-19 all'interno del corpo umano. La concentrazione di questi composti necessaria per ottenere un effetto antivirale significativo è spesso molto superiore a quella che può essere assunta realisticamente attraverso l'alimentazione. Inoltre, i complessi meccanismi delle infezioni virali richiedono interventi medici mirati, non solo agenti antimicrobici di vasto spettro.

La chiarificazione dell'OMS sottolinea l'importanza di affidarsi alla medicina basata sull'evidenza e di consultare professionisti sanitari per informazioni accurate sulle misure di prevenzione e trattamento del COVID-19. Sebbene una dieta sana, inclusi l'aglio, possa contribuire al benessere generale e a un sistema immunitario forte, non dovrebbe essere considerata una sostituzione per misure preventive provate come la vaccinazione, l'uso della mascherina e il distanziamento sociale, o per trattamenti medici stabiliti prescritti da professionisti sanitari qualificati. L'organizzazione continua a invitare il pubblico a essere vigilante contro le informazioni false e a cercare fonti attendibili durante la pandemia in corso.

La OMS advierte contra la desinformación sobre tratamientos alternativos y recalca la importancia de seguir medidas basadas en evidencia, como la vacunación y el distanciamiento social, en lugar de remedios no comprobados.

## Fake Government Website Used to Steal User Data: Beware of Phishing Scam

A new phishing scam is targeting internet users by impersonating a federal government website in an attempt to steal personal information. While the specific agency being impersonated is currently unconfirmed, reports indicate the fraudulent website closely mimics an official government portal, making it difficult for unsuspecting individuals to differentiate between the real and the fake.

This type of scam, known as phishing, relies on deceptive tactics to lure users into divulging sensitive data, such as social security numbers, bank account details, and passwords. By creating a convincing replica of a trusted website, scammers aim to trick users into believing they are interacting with a legitimate entity.

The consequences of falling victim to such a scam can be severe. Stolen personal information can be used for identity theft, financial fraud, and other criminal activities. Victims may find their credit scores damaged, their bank accounts emptied, and their identities compromised.

It is crucial for internet users to exercise caution when encountering websites requesting personal information, particularly those claiming to be affiliated with government agencies. Experts recommend several steps to protect against these scams:

*   **Double-check the URL:** Ensure the website address is accurate and matches the official URL of the government agency. Look for subtle misspellings or variations that could indicate a fake site.
*   **Verify the SSL Certificate:** Check for the "lock" icon in the address bar, indicating a secure connection (HTTPS). While this doesn't guarantee authenticity, it's a basic security measure.
*   **Be Wary of Unsolicited Requests:** Government agencies rarely request sensitive information via email or unsolicited online forms. Be suspicious of any unexpected requests for personal details.
*   **Report Suspicious Activity:** If you suspect a website is fraudulent, report it to the relevant authorities, such as the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) or the Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

By staying vigilant and employing these precautionary measures, individuals can significantly reduce their risk of falling victim to these increasingly sophisticated phishing scams. Protecting personal information online requires constant awareness and a healthy dose of skepticism.

Duke krijuar një kopje të sigurtë të një sajtë të përkushtuar, kallëzuesit shpresojnë të kujdesin përdoruesit të konsiderojnë se janë duke interaguar me një entitet të vërtetë.

## Misinformation Swirls Around Queensland Premier's Flu Shot

Social media has been awash with claims misidentifying Queensland Premier Annastacia Palaszczuk and falsely claiming she avoided receiving a COVID-19 vaccine. A video circulating online depicts Premier Palaszczuk receiving an injection, but misleading captions and commentary have created a storm of disinformation.

The individual in the video is indeed Annastacia Palaszczuk, the Premier of Queensland, a state situated in northeastern Australia. Contrary to claims circulating online, the video does not depict Premier Palaszczuk receiving a COVID-19 vaccine. Rather, the footage shows her getting vaccinated against the seasonal flu.

The confusion appears to stem from misidentification and the deliberate distortion of facts. The video, initially intended to promote influenza vaccination within the state, has been repurposed with false captions suggesting the Premier feigned receiving a COVID-19 vaccine.

Further complicating matters, some social media users have claimed Premier Palaszczuk avoided vaccination altogether. These claims are demonstrably false. Multiple sources, including other video recordings and photographic evidence from the same event, clearly show the Premier receiving the flu shot. This evidence discredits the assertion that she avoided the injection.

This incident highlights the ease with which misinformation can spread online, particularly within the context of public health. The manipulation of video content and the propagation of false narratives underscore the importance of verifying information from reputable sources before sharing it on social media. As public health campaigns continue and vaccine rollouts progress, combating misinformation remains crucial for ensuring accurate public understanding and fostering trust in public health initiatives.

## WHO Updates Guidance, Recommends Masks for General Public to Combat COVID-19 Spread

On June 5th, the World Health Organization (WHO) released updated guidance regarding the use of medical and fabric masks, advising the general public, including healthy individuals, to wear them as part of a comprehensive approach to mitigating the spread of the novel coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, responsible for the COVID-19 pandemic.

The new guidance marks a shift in the WHO's stance on mask usage. Initially, the organization primarily recommended masks for healthcare workers, individuals showing symptoms of COVID-19, and those caring for infected persons. The updated recommendations reflect a growing understanding of the virus's transmission dynamics, particularly the role of asymptomatic and pre-symptomatic spread.

The WHO emphasizes that mask-wearing is not a standalone solution, but rather one component within a broader strategy for controlling the pandemic. This strategy includes frequent handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based hand sanitizer, maintaining physical distancing of at least one meter (three feet), avoiding touching the face, practicing respiratory etiquette (coughing or sneezing into the elbow or a tissue), and ensuring adequate ventilation in indoor spaces.

The updated guidance covers both medical masks (also known as surgical masks) and non-medical or fabric masks. While medical masks are prioritized for healthcare workers and those at high risk, the WHO acknowledges the role of fabric masks in reducing transmission within the general population, especially in settings where physical distancing is difficult to maintain, such as public transportation, crowded shops, or workplaces.

The WHO provides detailed advice on the proper use and care of masks, regardless of type. This includes ensuring the mask covers the nose and mouth, washing hands before putting it on and after taking it off, avoiding touching the mask while wearing it, and properly disposing of or laundering reusable masks.

The WHO's revised guidance aims to provide clear and consistent advice to governments and individuals worldwide on how to best protect themselves and others from COVID-19. By incorporating mask-wearing into a comprehensive public health strategy, the WHO hopes to contribute to slowing the spread of the virus and ultimately bringing the pandemic under control. The organisation stresses the importance of context, stating that mask policies should be adapted to local epidemiology and resource availability.

## WHO নৱ পদ্ধতি প্ৰকাশ কৰিলে, সাধাৰণ মানুহক মাস্ক পৰামৰ্শ দিলে কোভিড-১৯ ছড়ী প্ৰসাৰ বিপদ পৰা বাঁচিবলৈ

২০ জুন তাৰিখে বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠন (WHO) মেডিকেল আৰু পাটৰ মাস্কৰ ব্যৱহাৰৰ বিষয়ে নৱ পদ্ধতি প্ৰকাশ কৰিলে আৰু সাধাৰণ মানুহ, যিহেতু তেওঁলোক স্বাস্থ্য পৰীক্ষা কৰা মানুহ আৰু কোভিড-১৯ আক্ৰান্ত মানুহৰ সাথে যোগাযোগ কৰা মানুহৰ বাহিৰেও মাস্ক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰাৰ পৰামৰ্শ দিলে কোভিড-১৯ মহামার্গৰ বিপদ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণ কৰিবলৈ এটা পূৰ্ণ পদ্ধতিৰ অংগ হিচাপে।

নতুন পদ্ধতিটো বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠনৰ মাস্ক ব্যৱহাৰৰ পৰামৰ্শ পৰিবৰ্তন ঘটাইছে। আগৰ কালত সংগঠনটো প্ৰাধান্য দিছিল চিকিৎসক, কোভিড-১৯ৰ লক্ষণ দেখা মানুহ আৰু আক্ৰান্ত মানুহৰ সাথে যোগাযোগ কৰা মানুহৰ বাবে মাস্ক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা। নতুন পৰামৰ্শ বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠনৰ দৃষ্টিভঙ্গিৰ পৰিবৰ্তন প্ৰতিফলিত কৰে, যাতে ছড়ীৰ প্ৰসাৰৰ প্ৰক্ৰিয়া, বিশেষত সিম্প্টম বিহীন আৰু পূৰ্ব সিম্প্টম সময়ত ছড়ী প্ৰসাৰৰ ভূমিকা আছে সেই বিষয়ত স্পষ্ট বুজা হৈছে।

বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠনে মাস্ক ব্যৱহাৰ একমাত্ৰ উপায় নহয় বুলি উল্লেখ কৰিছে, বিপদ নিয়ন্ত্ৰণৰ পৰিপৰিক স্ট্ৰাটেজীৰ এটা অংগ হিচাপে কাম কৰে। এই স্ট্ৰাটেজী শুদ্ধ হাত ধুই সাবান আৰু পানী বা আলকোহল ভিত্তিক হাত ধুৱালৈ যাওক, কমপক্ষে এ মিটাৰ (তিনি ফিট) দূৰত্ব বজাই থাকোক, চোৰাচুৰি নকৰক চুমকি আৰু চুমুকি কৰিবলৈ হাতৰ আঁৱৰ বা পাতৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰক আৰু ভিতৰৰ স্থানত সঠিক বাতাস বিস্তাৰ কৰক বুলি উল্লেখ কৰিছে।

নতুন পদ্ধতিটো মেডিকেল মাস্ক (বা চিকিৎসা মাস্ক) আৰু নন-মেডিকেল বা পাটৰ মাস্ক উভয় বিষয় আছে। যদিও মেডিকেল মাস্ক চিকিৎসক আৰু বিশেষ জৰুৰী কৰ্মী বাবে প্ৰাধান্য দিয়া হৈছে, বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠনে পাটৰ মাস্কৰ ভূমিকা স্বীকৃত কৰিছে যাতে সাধাৰণ মানুহৰ মাজত ছড়ী প্ৰসাৰ কমাই তুলিব পাৰে, বিশেষকৈ যাপন কৰিব নোৱাৰা স্থান যেনে জনসাংখ্যিক বাজাৰ, পাবলিক পৰিবহন আৰু কাৰ্যস্থল।

বিশ্ব আৰু স্বাস্থ্য সংগঠনে মাস্কৰ সঠিক ব্যৱহাৰ আৰু পৰিচৰ্যাৰ বিষয়ে বিস্তৃত পৰামৰ্শ প্ৰকাশ কৰিছে, বিশেষকৈ মাস্কটো চোৱা আৰু ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিব পৰামৰ্শ দিছে। এই পৰামৰ্শ হাত ধুই মাস্কটো পোৱা আৰু ব্যৱহাৰ কৰোৱাৰ আগত হাত ধুই থাকিব লাগে, মাস্ক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰাত হাত ছোৱা নাই আৰু পুনৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিবলৈ পৰিচৰ্যা কৰিব বা পুনৰ প্ৰস্তুত কৰিব পৰামৰ্শ দিছে।

## No Scientific Link Between Ivermectin Use and COVID-19 Decline in Natal, Brazil

Claims circulating online suggesting a connection between ivermectin use and a decrease in COVID-19 infections in Natal, Rio Grande do Norte (RN), and other municipalities in Brazil are unsubstantiated by scientific evidence, according to experts.

The social media post circulating, translated from Portuguese, explicitly states, "There is no study that relates the decrease in the number of people infected by Covid-19 in Natal (RN), or in any municipality of Brazil, to the use of ivermectin as a form of treatment." This assertion highlights the lack of credible research supporting the notion that ivermectin contributed to the decline in COVID-19 cases.

This comes amid a global discussion surrounding the potential efficacy of ivermectin as a treatment for COVID-19. Despite its approval for use in treating parasitic infections, numerous studies and health organizations worldwide, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in the United States, have consistently stated that there is no conclusive evidence to support the use of ivermectin for the prevention or treatment of COVID-19.

These organizations emphasize the need for rigorous, large-scale clinical trials to properly assess the drug's efficacy and safety in the context of the virus. Furthermore, they caution against the potential for adverse effects associated with ivermectin use, especially when taken in dosages that are not medically supervised.

While anecdotal reports and observational data may exist, these do not constitute sufficient scientific proof to establish a causal relationship between ivermectin use and the reduction of COVID-19 cases in Natal or any other Brazilian municipality. Factors such as vaccination rates, public health measures like mask mandates and social distancing, and natural fluctuations in the virus's transmission patterns likely played a more significant role in observed declines in infection rates. Therefore, attributing the decrease in COVID-19 infections solely or significantly to ivermectin use is misleading and lacks scientific backing.

## Coronavirus Virus Particles Detected in Wastewater, but Transmission Risk Remains Low

Recent reports have highlighted the detection of coronavirus particles in wastewater systems. While concerning at first glance, experts assure the public that there is currently no evidence to suggest the virus can be transmitted through sewage water.

The presence of viral RNA in wastewater isn't entirely unexpected. Individuals infected with COVID-19 can shed the virus through bodily fluids, including feces. These fluids eventually make their way into the sewage system. Detecting viral fragments in this water is a testament to the sensitivity and accuracy of modern testing methods.

However, detection of viral RNA doesn't equate to infectivity. The presence of genetic material alone doesn't mean that infectious virus particles are present and viable. The virus may be inactive or significantly degraded during its passage through the digestive system and the wastewater treatment process.

Health organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) have consistently stated that the primary mode of transmission for COVID-19 is through respiratory droplets produced when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Direct contact with contaminated surfaces is also considered a possible, though less common, transmission route.

While research into the behavior of the virus in wastewater is ongoing, the current scientific consensus remains that the risk of contracting COVID-19 through sewage systems is extremely low. Proper hygiene practices, like frequent handwashing, continue to be the most effective methods of preventing transmission. Monitoring wastewater for viral RNA is being explored as a potential early warning system for outbreaks within communities, but it is not indicative of a direct threat to public health via the water system.

## Cząstki wirusa koronawirusa wykryte w ściekach, ale ryzyko transmisji pozostaje niskie

Ostatnie raporty podkreślają wykrycie cząstek wirusa koronawirusa w systemach ściekowych. Choć wydaje się to zaskakujące, ekspertom można zaufać, że obecnie nie ma dowodów wskazujących na możliwość przenoszenia wirusa przez wody ściekowe.

Obecność RNA wirusa w ściekach nie jest całkowicie zaskakująca. Osoby zakażone koronawirusem mogą odpadanie wirusa przez cieczki organizmu, w tym stolicę. Te cieczki w końcu trafiają do systemu ściekowego. Wykrywanie fragmentów wirusa w takiej wodzie jest dowodem na wysoką czułość i dokładność nowoczesnych metod testowania.

Jednak wykrycie RNA wirusa nie oznacza jego zakaźności. Obecność materii genetycznej sama w sobie nie oznacza obecności cząstek zakaźnych i aktywnych. Wirus może być nieaktywny lub znacznie rozłożony podczas przemieszczania się przez układ trawienny oraz procesy oczyszczania ścieków.

Organizacje zdrowotne, takie jak Organizacja Światowa Zdrowia (WHO) i Centrum Kontroli i Zapobiegania Chorobom (CDC), zgodnie z wyraźnym stwierdzeniem, że głównym sposobem przenoszenia się COVID-19 są krople oddechowe wydzielane przez osoby zakażone, kiedy kaszą lub kaszle. Kontakt bezpośredni z zanieczyszczonymi powierzchniami również jest uważany za możliwy, choć mniej typowy, sposób przenoszenia się choroby.

Choć badania dotyczące zachowania wirusa w ściekach trwają, obecny konsensus naukowy nadal wskazuje, że ryzyko przeniesienia się COVID-19 poprzez systemy ściekowe jest bardzo niskie. Poprawne praktyki higieniczne, takie jak częste mycie rąk, nadal pozostają najskuteczniejszymi sposobami zapobiegania przenoszeniu się choroby. Monitorowanie ścieków w celu wykrywania RNA wirusa jest badane jako potencjalny system wczesnego ostrzeżenia dotyczącego wybuchów chorób w społecznościach, ale nie wskazuje bezpośredniego zagrożenia dla zdrowia publicznego poprzez system wodny.

## Looking Back: Veja's 2003 Cover Story Spotlighted the SARS Epidemic

A recent observation on social media highlighted the focus of the May 7, 2003, cover story of the prominent Brazilian news magazine, Veja. The post correctly pointed out that the cover feature that week delved into the unfolding global crisis surrounding Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS).

At the time, the SARS epidemic, which emerged in late 2002 and continued through 2003, was a source of significant global concern. The novel respiratory illness, caused by the SARS-associated coronavirus (SARS-CoV), spread rapidly across international borders, infecting thousands and causing hundreds of deaths. The virus originated in Guangdong province in Southern China and quickly spread to other Asian countries, including Hong Kong, Singapore, and Vietnam, before reaching North America and Europe.

Veja's decision to dedicate its cover story to SARS in May 2003 reflects the gravity of the situation and the impact it was having worldwide. The magazine likely explored various aspects of the epidemic, including its origins, transmission routes, symptoms, and potential treatments. They would have likely investigated the measures being taken by global health organizations like the World Health Organization (WHO) to contain the spread of the virus and provide guidance to affected countries.

The 2003 SARS outbreak served as a stark reminder of the potential for novel infectious diseases to rapidly spread across the globe, disrupting daily life and posing a significant threat to public health. Veja's coverage played a critical role in informing the Brazilian public about the disease, its potential risks, and the ongoing efforts to combat it. This historical context provides valuable insight into how the world responded to a previous coronavirus outbreak, offering lessons that remain relevant in the face of contemporary global health challenges. The magazine's cover story stands as a time capsule, capturing the anxieties and responses surrounding a serious epidemic from two decades ago.

**Federal Chamber Approves Measures to Protect Women Victims of Domestic Violence During Pandemic**

Brasilia, Brazil – The Brazilian Chamber of Deputies approved two bills, PL 1444/2020 and PL 1552/2020, on Thursday, [insert date if known, otherwise: last Thursday, October 9th]. These bills focus on providing essential protections for women who are victims of domestic violence, especially during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

The approval of these bills comes at a time when concerns are growing about the increased vulnerability of women facing abuse, exacerbated by lockdowns and social isolation measures implemented to combat the spread of the virus. Quarantine measures have inadvertently trapped many women in potentially dangerous situations with their abusers, limiting their access to support networks and resources.

While specific details of the measures included in PL 1444/2020 and PL 1552/2020 were not immediately available, the general objective is to reinforce existing protections and provide additional support to women experiencing domestic violence during this unprecedented crisis. The approval signals a recognition by the Brazilian government of the critical need to address the rising risk of domestic violence during the pandemic.

Following the approval of the bills in the Chamber of Deputies, they will now proceed to the Senate for further consideration and potential approval. If passed by the Senate, the legislation will then be sent to the President for final approval and enactment into law.

Following the approval of the bills, information was disseminated to clarify a point of public concern. Specific rumors had circulated alleging that either PL 1444/2020 or PL 1552/2020 contained provisions related to the legalization of abortion in Brazil, specifically allowing abortions for pregnant women up to 22 weeks of gestation. These rumors were specifically addressed after the vote. According to sources close to the legislation, neither bill contains any measures addressing the legal status of abortion in Brazil. The bills are solely focused on domestic violence prevention and victim protection, aiming to address the urgent need for support services during the ongoing public health crisis.

**Bundeshaus genehmigt Maßnahmen zur Schutz von Frauenopfern häuslicher Gewalt während der Pandemie**

Brasilia, Brasilien – Das brasilianische Abgeordnetenhaus hat am Donnerstag, [Datum einfügen, falls bekannt, andernfalls: letzte Woche, den 9. Oktober], die beiden Gesetzesvorschläge PL 1444/2020 und PL 1552/2020 genehmigt. Diese Gesetze zielen darauf ab, grundlegende Schutzmaßnahmen für Frauen zu gewährleisten, die Opfer häuslicher Gewalt sind, insbesondere während der aktuellen COVID-19-Pandemie.

Die Genehmigung dieser Gesetze erfolgt zu einer Zeit, in der sich Sorgen um die zunehmende Verletzlichkeit von Frauen, die Gewalt erleben, vermehren, was durch Lockdowns und soziale Isolationsmaßnahmen, die zur Eindämmung der Virusverbreitung ergriffen wurden, verschärft wird. Quarantäne-Maßnahmen haben viele Frauen unabsichtlich in potenziell gefährliche Situationen mit ihren Tätern verpflanzt und ihre Zugangsmöglichkeiten zu Unterstützungsnetzwerken und Ressourcen eingeschränkt.

Obwohl konkrete Details der in PL 1444/2020 und PL 1552/2020 enthaltenen Maßnahmen zunächst nicht verfügbar waren, hat das allgemeine Ziel darin bestanden, bestehende Schutzmaßnahmen zu stärken und zusätzliche Unterstützung für Frauen zu bieten, die häusliche Gewalt erleben, während dieser außergewöhnlichen Krise. Die Genehmigung signalisiert eine Anerkennung durch die brasilianische Regierung der dringenden Notwendigkeit, den steigenden Risiken häuslicher Gewalt während der Pandemie entgegenzutreten.

Nach der Genehmigung der Gesetze im Abgeordnetenhaus werden diese nun im Senat weiter betrachtet und ggf. genehmigt. Falls der Senat die Gesetze verabschiedet, wird die Gesetzgebung anschließend dem Präsidenten zur endgültigen Genehmigung und Verkündung als Gesetz übermittelt.

Nach der Genehmigung der Gesetze wurde Information verbreitet, um eine öffentliche Bedenken zu klären. Es hatte sich Gerüchte verbreitet, wonach entweder PL 1444/2020 oder PL 1552/2020 Bestimmungen enthielten, die die Legalisierung von Abtreibungen in Brasilien betreffen würden, insbesondere Abtreibungen für schwangere Frauen bis zu 22 Wochen Schwangerschaft. Diese Gerüchte wurden nach der Abstimmung adressiert. Laut Quellen, die eng mit der Gesetzgebung verbunden sind, enthalten weder der Gesetzesvorschlag PL 1444/2020 noch PL 1552/2020 Maßnahmen zur rechtlichen Stellung der Abtreibung in Brasilien. Die Gesetze sind ausschließlich auf die Prävention häuslicher Gewalt und den Schutz der Opfer ausgerichtet, um den dringenden Bedarf an Unterstützungsleistungen während der aktuellen öffentlichen Gesundheitskrise zu beantworten.

## Parisian Hospital Staff Protested Working Conditions Weeks Before First COVID-19 Case

A video resurfaced recently showing medical professionals at the Hospital Saint-Louis in Paris protesting poor working conditions, highlighting the strain already placed on France’s public healthcare system before the arrival of the COVID-19 pandemic. The video, originally posted on Twitter by French doctor Bernard Jomier on January 14, 2020, captured the demonstration.

The protests, staged by hospital staff, reflected a broader discontent within the French public healthcare sector at the time. Healthcare workers had been voicing concerns about understaffing, lack of resources, and overall deterioration of working conditions for months leading up to the January 2020 demonstration. These systemic issues placed significant pressure on medical personnel and, as the video shows, prompted direct action.

While the world was largely unaware of the impending global pandemic at the time of the protest, the video provides a crucial glimpse into the vulnerabilities already present within France’s healthcare infrastructure. Notably, the first confirmed case of COVID-19 in France wasn’t reported until ten days later, on January 24, 2020. This timing underscores that the issues being raised were not related to the pandemic, but rather pre-existing problems that would undoubtedly be exacerbated by the unprecedented health crisis that followed.

The video's resurgence serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by healthcare workers globally. It emphasizes the importance of addressing systemic issues within healthcare systems to ensure they are equipped to handle both everyday demands and unexpected crises. The protests captured in the video highlight the critical need for investment in public health and the wellbeing of those who dedicate their lives to providing care.

## A Year On: Reflecting on a Midsummer Day in July 2020

July 17th, 2020. A seemingly ordinary date, yet one that lingers in the collective memory as a point of reference in a year unlike any other. While details specific to that date are scarce, the very mention of "17/07/2020" immediately conjures images of a world grappling with the unprecedented challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic.

By this mid-July date, the pandemic was well underway, having drastically altered daily life across the globe. Lockdowns, travel restrictions, and social distancing measures were becoming commonplace, reshaping how people worked, socialized, and even shopped. The economic impact was significant, with businesses struggling and unemployment rates soaring in many countries.

Beyond the practical adjustments, the date also symbolizes a period of heightened uncertainty and anxiety. The virus was still largely unknown, and the race to develop effective treatments and vaccines was just beginning. News headlines were dominated by rising infection rates, hospital overcrowding, and heartbreaking stories of loss.

The summer of 2020 was also marked by social unrest and political polarization in many nations. Protests against racial injustice, sparked by high-profile incidents of police brutality, were sweeping across the United States and resonating globally. These movements amplified existing societal tensions and fueled debates about systemic inequality.

Reflecting on July 17th, 2020, therefore, is not about remembering a single event, but rather about acknowledging the complex and multifaceted context of that time. It's a reminder of the profound impact the pandemic had on individuals and communities, the economic hardships it created, and the social and political upheavals it exacerbated. While the world has undoubtedly changed since then, understanding the significance of dates like July 17th, 2020, is crucial for navigating the challenges of the present and building a more resilient future.

## Oxford Vaccine Trials Underway in Brazil, Fiocruz Confirms

Rio de Janeiro - The Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz), a prominent Brazilian public health institution, has released a statement clarifying the development and current status of the Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine in Brazil. According to a press release from Fiocruz's press office, the vaccine was jointly developed by the University of Oxford and pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca.

The clarification comes at a crucial time as the global race for a safe and effective COVID-19 vaccine intensifies. Fiocruz, a key player in Brazil's public health infrastructure, is deeply involved in the efforts to combat the pandemic within the country.

The statement specifically highlights the ongoing Phase 3 clinical trials of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine in Brazil. Phase 3 trials are a critical step in vaccine development, involving large-scale testing to assess the vaccine's efficacy, identify potential side effects, and confirm its safety for widespread use. These trials are essential for regulatory approval and eventual distribution to the public.

Brazil has emerged as a key location for conducting Phase 3 trials for several potential COVID-19 vaccines due to the significant impact of the virus within the country, providing a robust environment for assessing vaccine efficacy. The involvement of Fiocruz in these trials underlines Brazil's commitment to participating in the global effort to find a solution to the pandemic. The data gathered from these trials will be crucial in determining the overall effectiveness and safety profile of the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine, contributing significantly to the worldwide fight against COVID-19. The ongoing trials are being closely monitored by both Brazilian and international health authorities.

Río de Janeiro – Oswaldo Cruzová fond (Fiocruz), významná brazílska verejná zdravotnícka inštitúcia, vyhlásil stanovisko, ktoré vysvetľuje vývoj a aktuálny stav vakcíny Oxford-AstraZeneca proti ochoreniu COVID-19 v Brazílii. Podľa tlačové správy z tlačového oddelenia Fiocruz sa vakcína spoločne vyvíjala Univerzitou v Oxforde a farmaceutickým gigantom AstraZenecou.

Toto stanovisko sa objavilo v dôležitý moment, keď sa globálny súťaž o bezpečnú a účinnú vakcínu proti ochoreniu COVID-19 zintenzívni. Fiocruz, kľúčová inštitúcia v brazílskej verejnej zdravotníckej infraštruktúre, sa zúčastňuje snažení bojovať proti pandémii v rámci krajiny.

Stanovisko výslovně zdôrazňuje prebiehajúce fázy 3 klinických skúšok vakcíny Oxford-AstraZeneca v Brazílii. Fáza 3 klinických skúšok je kritickým krokom v vývoji vakcíny, pri ktorom sa vykonáva masívne testovanie na overenie účinnosti vakcíny, identifikáciu potenciálnych vedľajších účinkov a potvrdenie jej bezpečnosti pre široké použitie. Tieto skúšky sú základom pre správne schválenie a následné rozdelenie vakcíny na verejné použitie.

Brazília sa stala dôležitým miestom pre vykonávanie fázy 3 skúšok viacerých potenciálnych vakcíny proti ochoreniu COVID-19, dôvodom je významný dopad ochorenia na krajine, čo poskytuje silný prostredie na hodnotenie účinnosti vakcíny. Zúčastnenie Fiocruz v týchto skúškach podčiarkuje Brazíliu záväzok podieľať sa na globálnom pokusu nájsť riešenie pre pandémiu. Dáta z týchto skúšok budú kľúčové pri určení celkovej účinnosti a bezpečnostnej profil vakcíny Oxford-AstraZeneca, čo prispieje významne k globálnemu boju proti ochoreniu COVID-19. Prebiehajúce skúšky sú prísnym sledovaním aj brazílskych aj mezinárodných zdravotníckych orgánov.

**Philosopher Cortella Denies Authorship of Widely Circulated Text**

Brazilian philosopher Mario Sergio Cortella has taken to social media to publicly deny authorship of a text circulating online under the title “Que Tire La Primera Piedra” (Let He Who is Without Sin Cast the First Stone). In a recent Facebook post on his personal account, Cortella clarified that the piece, often attributed to him, is not his work.

“A text about ‘que tire la primera piedra’ is circulating on the internet as if it were my authorship. It is not,” Cortella stated in his concise but decisive message.

The post comes as a direct response to the apparent widespread misattribution of the text, highlighting a common problem in the digital age: the ease with which information, and especially authorship, can be distorted online. While Cortella doesn't specify the exact content of the text in question, the popularity of the "que tire la primera piedra" phrase suggests it likely deals with themes of judgment, morality, and the importance of self-reflection before criticizing others. The saying itself originates from a passage in the Bible (John 8:7), where Jesus challenges a crowd preparing to stone a woman accused of adultery.

The philosopher's decision to publicly address the misattribution underscores the importance he places on maintaining the integrity of his intellectual work. It also serves as a reminder to consumers of online content to be critical and to verify the source of information before sharing it, especially when dealing with philosophical or insightful texts often credited to prominent figures. While the specific content of the misattributed piece remains unclear without further investigation, Cortella's statement clearly separates himself from the online material and alerts his followers to the inaccurate claim of authorship.

## Misinformation Circulates Regarding Homicide Authorship in Brazil

A recent social media post has been circulating, containing inaccurate information about the authorship of homicides in Brazil. The claim suggests a definitive national statistic exists regarding the perpetrators of these crimes. However, this information is false and lacks factual basis.

In reality, a comprehensive national dataset on homicide authorship does not exist. The core reason for this is the unfortunate reality that in the majority of homicide cases across the country, the perpetrator remains unidentified. This poses a significant challenge for law enforcement and data collection efforts seeking to understand the dynamics of violent crime.

The social media post in question specifically cites a figure of 13.9%, incorrectly attributing it to national homicide authorship statistics. Further investigation reveals that this figure originates from a report by the UOL news portal. However, the report, and the 13.9% statistic, refers specifically to the *victims* of homicides in the state of Rio Grande do Sul, and not the perpetrators, as the misleading social media post suggests. The UOL report, likely focusing on demographic data of homicide victims within Rio Grande do Sul, has been misconstrued and amplified through social media, leading to widespread misinformation.

This instance highlights the importance of verifying information, especially when it pertains to sensitive topics such as crime and public safety. The absence of a national database on homicide authorship underscores the challenges faced by Brazil in addressing violent crime effectively. Accurate data is crucial for formulating informed policies and allocating resources to combat this problem. Therefore, responsible sharing of information and critical evaluation of sources are essential in preventing the spread of misleading narratives.

## Masks Don't Reduce Oxygen Levels, Debunking Misinformation

A recent social media post has addressed and debunked a common misconception surrounding the use of face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic: the claim that they significantly reduce oxygen intake or lead to blood acidification. The post clarifies that wearing masks does *not* cause a 20% reduction in oxygen levels or create a dangerous build-up of carbon dioxide in the bloodstream.

This assertion, often repeated online, stems from a misunderstanding of how masks function and the physiological processes of breathing. The post highlights a crucial distinction: significant oxygen deprivation only occurs when airflow is completely blocked, creating an airtight seal. Common face masks, whether surgical masks, cloth masks, or even N95 respirators (when not professionally fitted), do *not* create such a seal. They allow for the passage of air, albeit filtered, preventing a dangerous build-up of carbon dioxide and ensuring adequate oxygen intake.

The circulation of this misinformation has led to unnecessary fear and resistance to mask-wearing, a vital public health measure recommended by medical experts worldwide to prevent the spread of the novel coronavirus. These masks act as a barrier, significantly reducing the transmission of respiratory droplets that carry the virus, thereby protecting both the wearer and those around them.

The persistence of this myth emphasizes the importance of relying on credible sources of information from health organizations and scientific experts. It is crucial to understand that wearing masks is a safe and effective way to help combat the ongoing pandemic and protect vulnerable populations. Claims suggesting otherwise should be critically examined and dismissed when lacking scientific backing.

Ақырғы социалдық медиа посты, әлемдік пандемия кезіндегі маскаларды қолдану барысында пайда болатын бір жиі кездесетін қате білімді қайта айқындауға арналған. Пост, маскаларды қолдану қаныққан ауаның 20% деңгейін қысқартпайтын, қанда қауіпті қарбидік қышқылдың құбылысын туғызбайды деген нәтижеге жетеді.

Бұл тұжырым, көптеген онлайн платформаларда қайталанып жүрген, маскалардың қызмет ететін әдісін және тыныс алу физиологиялық үрдістерін түсінбеу нәтижесінде пайда болған.
